title: AWS Weekly Roundup: AgentCore Runtime V2, Amazon DynamoDB bulk put items, and more (November 9, 2026)
body: AWS Weekly Roundup: AgentCore Runtime V2, Amazon DynamoDB bulk put items, and more (November 9, 2026) Most of the cost of adopting something new isn’t the new thing, it’s the move. Moving a Hive table to Apache Iceberg has typically meant weeks of engineering work. Last week, Amazon S3 Tables turned that into three steps: start, sync as often as you need, complete. The source stays writable except for a few minutes at cutover. The same week, Amazon DynamoDB started loading data from S3 into tables that already exist. The pattern I like is that neither one asks you to stop what’s running. That’s also the way to read the agent news this week. The new Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime is a single field on the runtime you already have, and Web Answer is a tool you attach to a gateway you already run. Now, let’s get into this week’s AWS news… Headlines The new AgentCore Runtime: elastic, optimized, and consistently fast starts – If you run agents on AgentCore and haven’t tried the new runtime since it became generally available, it’s worth a look. It changes two things. First, memory: sessions start small, page in more on demand, and give memory back when it goes cold instead of holding the peak, so you pay for what your agent uses. Second, cold starts: AgentCore prepares your environment once, snapshots it, and restores the snapshot for every new instance. In the team’s tests, that kept P75 cold starts at about 2 seconds for images from 200 MB up to 2 GB, while the original runtime rose from roughly 5.4 seconds to nearly 30 seconds as images grew. The per-unit rate is higher, but you use far fewer GB-hours, so the team expects most agents to see a lower bill, though that isn’t guaranteed. To opt in, you set platformVersion to V2 when you create or update a runtime. Create and update take several minutes while the snapshot is prepared, and your container must report healthy on /ping within 120 seconds, so report health only after initialization finishes. The docs cover how to optimize your agent for V2 . V2 is available in 10 Regions , and committed baseline pricing is coming soon. Amazon S3 Tables now offer managed migration of Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg – You can now migrate Parquet tables registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog into S3 Tables without building a pipeline or provisioning compute. S3 Tables validates the source and produces a compatibility report covering every object in scope. Each sync copies only what changed, so production keeps writing until cutover. Afterward you can query the table with Amazon Athena , Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio , or any engine that speaks the Iceberg REST API. You pay only for the data copied, with no charge for the conversion, and objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering keep their tier. At launch it works within the same account and Region, in 10 Regions. Last week’s launches Here are some launches and updates from this past week that caught my attention: Amazon DynamoDB now supports bulk put items – You can now load line-delimited DynamoDB JSON or Amazon Ion files from Amazon S3 into existing tables as a managed, asynchronous job. Each record can carry its own condition expression, so one file can mix plain, insert-only, and version-guarded writes. Writes use dedicated system capacity and cost less than the equivalent per-request writes. An Accelerated tier handles deadline-bound jobs. The Database blog post gives illustrative Accelerated times of less than 1 hour for 100 million 1 KB items. One thing to know before you start: canceling doesn’t roll back items already written. Announcing Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – You can now give an agent a single tool call that returns a synthesized, cited answer to a natural-language question, instead of building your own search, retrieval, and citation pipeline. Web Answer plans its own searches, runs several in parallel, and decides when it has enough evidence. You attach it as a target on AgentCore Gateway and call it over MCP, and you can limit it with domain include and deny lists and publish-date filters. It’s available in US East (N. Virginia). The getting started post explains when to use it instead of Web Search, which returns ranked results for your own model to synthesize. AWS Lambda now supports queues for Apache Kafka in self-managed Kafka event sources – You can now process records from a single Kafka partition across many parallel AWS Lambda invocations. Classic consumer groups cap parallelism at the partition count. Queue mode uses Kafka share groups and needs Kafka 4.2 or later with share groups enabled. It works with self-managed clusters and managed offerings such as Confluent Cloud. You give up ordering and get at-least-once delivery, so your functions need to be idempotent. The Compute blog walkthrough covers poller scaling and when to keep stream mode. AWS announces AWS Interconnect – last mile preview with Equinix – You can now set up a private, managed connection from Equinix’s network of 282 data centers to AWS without ordering cross-connects or configuring routers. Capacity is quad-redundant across two locations and four links, with BGP and VLANs configured for you, a 99.99% availability SLA, and MACsec by default. You pick a Region, bandwidth, and AWS Direct Connect gateway, then paste the activation key into Equinix Fabric. The preview covers the San Jose metro and, as of last Thursday , Northern Virginia, with 1 Gbps connections at no charge. AWS Security Hub now provides an SBOM inventory for your compute resources – You can now see every software package installed across your organization’s Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon ECR images, and Lambda functions in AWS Security Hub , with each package’s version and how many resources run it. That’s the list you want the next time a widely used library has a vulnerability. The inventory builds on the SBOMs that Amazon Inspector already generates, so it fills in automatically wherever Inspector is enabled. It’s included in Security Hub Essentials at no additional cost. For a full list of AWS announcements, be sure to keep an eye on the What’s New with AWS page. Other AWS news Here are some additional posts and resources that you might find interesting: Serverless ICYMI Q3 2026 – Julian Wood’s quarterly recap is a quick serverless catch-up before re:Invent: Lambda SnapStart for container images, a 90-minute timeout on Lambda Managed Instances, Lambda MicroVMs in 10 Regions, 1 MiB payloads in Amazon SNS , and the new AgentCore Runtime. AWS contributes a large-transaction binary log optimization to MySQL – With binlog on, a huge transaction holds a global commit lock while its events are copied, blocking every other commit. The optimization, which Amazon Aurora MySQL has run in production since 2019, promotes the spill file into the binlog instead of copying it. In AWS’s tests, commit latency for a 50 GiB transaction dropped from about 7 minutes to about 2 to 2.5 seconds. It has now shipped to community MySQL. How OrderServ achieved up to 64% cost savings with multi-tenant ECS – Cognizant’s food-ordering platform went from one Amazon ECS cluster per brand on AWS Fargate to a shared cluster on EC2 Auto Scaling groups with warm pools. The 64% applies to a 3-year Compute Savings Plan (47% with a 1-year plan). Scaling time also fell from 5–7 minutes to 30–60 seconds. retained_feed_body: Most of the cost of adopting something new isn’t the new thing, it’s the move. Moving a Hive table to Apache Iceberg has typically meant weeks of engineering work. Last week, Amazon S3 Tables turned that into three steps: start, sync as often as you need, complete. The source stays writable except for a few minutes at cutover. The same week, Amazon DynamoDB started loading data from S3 into tables that already exist. The pattern I like is that neither one asks you to stop what’s running. That’s also the way to read the agent news this week. The new Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime is a single field on the runtime you already have, and Web Answer is a tool you attach to a gateway you already run. Now, let’s get into this week’s AWS news… Headlines The new AgentCore Runtime: elastic, optimized, and consistently fast starts – If you run agents on AgentCore and haven’t tried the new runtime since it became generally available, it’s worth a look. It changes two things. First, memory: sessions start small, page in more on demand, and give memory back when it goes cold instead of holding the peak, so you pay for what your agent uses. Second, cold starts: AgentCore prepares your environment once, snapshots it, and restores the snapshot for every new instance. In the team’s tests, that kept P75 cold starts at about 2 seconds for images from 200 MB up to 2 GB, while the original runtime rose from roughly 5.4 seconds to nearly 30 seconds as images grew. The per-unit rate is higher, but you use far fewer GB-hours, so the team expects most agents to see a lower bill, though that isn’t guaranteed. To opt in, you set platformVersion to V2 when you create or update a runtime. Create and update take several minutes while the snapshot is prepared, and your container must report healthy on /ping within 120 seconds, so report health only after initialization finishes. The docs cover how to optimize your agent for V2 . V2 is available in 10 Regions , and committed baseline pricing is coming soon. Amazon S3 Tables now offer managed migration of Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg – You can now migrate Parquet tables registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog into S3 Tables without building a pipeline or provisioning compute. S3 Tables validates the source and produces a compatibility report covering every object in scope. Each sync copies only what changed, so production keeps writing until cutover. Afterward you can query the table with Amazon Athena , Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio , or any engine that speaks the Iceberg REST API. You pay only for the data copied, with no charge for the conversion, and objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering keep their tier. At launch it works within the same account and Region, in 10 Regions. Last week’s launches Here are some launches and updates from this past week that caught my attention: Amazon DynamoDB now supports bulk put items – You can now load line-delimited DynamoDB JSON or Amazon Ion files from Amazon S3 into existing tables as a managed, asynchronous job. Each record can carry its own condition expression, so one file can mix plain, insert-only, and version-guarded writes. Writes use dedicated system capacity and cost less than the equivalent per-request writes. An Accelerated tier handles deadline-bound jobs. The Database blog post gives illustrative Accelerated times of less than 1 hour for 100 million 1 KB items. One thing to know before you start: canceling doesn’t roll back items already written. Announcing Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – You can now give an agent a single tool call that returns a synthesized, cited answer to a natural-language question, instead of building your own search, retrieval, and citation pipeline. Web Answer plans its own searches, runs several in parallel, and decides when it has enough evidence. You attach it as a target on AgentCore Gateway and call it over MCP, and you can limit it with domain include and deny lists and publish-date filters. It’s available in US East (N. Virginia). The getting started post explains when to use it instead of Web Search, which returns ranked results for your own model to synthesize. AWS Lambda now supports queues for Apache Kafka in self-managed Kafka event sources – You can now process records from a single Kafka partition across many parallel AWS Lambda invocations. Classic consumer groups cap parallelism at the partition count. Queue mode uses Kafka share groups and needs Kafka 4.2 or later with share groups enabled. It works with self-managed clusters and managed offerings such as Confluent Cloud. You give up ordering and get at-least-once delivery, so your functions need to be idempotent. The Compute blog walkthrough covers poller scaling and when to keep stream mode. AWS announces AWS Interconnect – last mile preview with Equinix – You can now set up a private, managed connection from Equinix’s network of 282 data centers to AWS without ordering cross-connects or configuring routers. Capacity is quad-redundant across two locations and four links, with BGP and VLANs configured for you, a 99.99% availability SLA, and MACsec by default. You pick a Region, bandwidth, and AWS Direct Connect gateway, then paste the activation key into Equinix Fabric. The preview covers the San Jose metro and, as of last Thursday , Northern Virginia, with 1 Gbps connections at no charge. AWS Security Hub now provides an SBOM inventory for your compute resources – You can now see every software package installed across your organization’s Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon ECR images, and Lambda functions in AWS Security Hub , with each package’s version and how many resources run it. That’s the list you want the next time a widely used library has a vulnerability. The inventory builds on the SBOMs that Amazon Inspector already generates, so it fills in automatically wherever Inspector is enabled. It’s included in Security Hub Essentials at no additional cost. For a full list of AWS announcements, be sure to keep an eye on the What’s New with AWS page. Other AWS news Here are some additional posts and resources that you might find interesting: Serverless ICYMI Q3 2026 – Julian Wood’s quarterly recap is a quick serverless catch-up before re:Invent: Lambda SnapStart for container images, a 90-minute timeout on Lambda Managed Instances, Lambda MicroVMs in 10 Regions, 1 MiB payloads in Amazon SNS , and the new AgentCore Runtime. AWS contributes a large-transaction binary log optimization to MySQL – With binlog on, a huge transaction holds a global commit lock while its events are copied, blocking every other commit. The optimization, which Amazon Aurora MySQL has run in production since 2019, promotes the spill file into the binlog instead of copying it. In AWS’s tests, commit latency for a 50 GiB transaction dropped from about 7 minutes to about 2 to 2.5 seconds. It has now shipped to community MySQL. How OrderServ achieved up to 64% cost savings with multi-tenant ECS – Cognizant’s food-ordering platform went from one Amazon ECS cluster per brand on AWS Fargate to a shared cluster on EC2 Auto Scaling groups with warm pools. The 64% applies to a 3-year Compute Savings Plan (47% with a 1-year plan). Scaling time also fell from 5–7 minutes to 30–60 seconds. title: Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation
body: Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation At the Conference on Robot Learning, NVIDIA is introducing GR00T 2, Isaac Lab 3.0 and new open benchmarks, built in collaboration with partners, bringing precision and scale to robot training. November 9, 2026 by Sasa Docca 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Simulation, which has long been the proving ground for robots learning to walk, roll and hop, is now helping researchers teach robots tasks that require a finer touch: aligning gears, connecting cables and assembling small components. The shift from locomotion to manipulation is taking center stage at this week’s Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, Texas, alongside the rise of agentic robotics — a new paradigm that integrates frontier agents to create interpretable code for physical robotics systems. At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing new open robotics technologies, including world action models , simulation tools, benchmarks and agentic workflows. Two NVIDIA papers are among six finalists out of thousands of submissions for the Best Paper Awards at CoRL: GRAIL (Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models), which presents a digital generation pipeline for 3D assets and simulator-ready scenes for robot learning. RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies , which introduces a robot model and training recipe that scales visuomotor context three orders of magnitude beyond state-of-the-art policies without growing inference latency. These advancements help researchers train robots on complex tasks, evaluate their performance across changing conditions and use failures to guide further learning — building the precision, adaptability and autonomy needed to move from lab demonstrations to industrial deployment. NVIDIA is working with partners like Ambi Robotics , Bosch Research , Dexmate , Dyna Robotics , FieldAI , Flexion , Noitom Robotics , Siemens , Skild AI , RLWRLD , UC Berkeley , Walden Robotics and the University of Washington to bring these advancements to the broader robotics community. World Action Models Enable Next Level of Robot Autonomy The next level of robot autonomy requires robots to perceive their surroundings, anticipate how their actions will change the environment and execute complex, multistep tasks with a high degree of precision. World action models enable exactly that. At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing GR00T 2 , an open frontier world action model built on NVIDIA Cosmos. Trained on diverse robot and human data, including 100,000 hours of NVIDIA open source human egocentric data , the model enables robots to learn dexterous manipulation skills. Key features include: Out-of-the-box performance: Completed 40 of 50 evaluated tasks at least once without task-specific demonstrations. Skill transfer: Learns from human demonstrations and transfers skills between different robot bodies without robot demonstrations Generalization with little data: Achieved 71% average success across 50 tasks with just one demonstration per task, increasing to 95% with five. Agent control: AI agents can use GR00T 2’s application programming interface and supporting tools to run skills in sequence and recover from errors. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/groot-2-shipping-label.mp4 GR00T 2 currently ranks among the top three models across all vision language action and world action model categories for the RoboCasa365, RoboLab, RoboDojo and MolmoSpaces benchmarks, with multiple leaderboard wins. Nexuni is testing it for robotic laundry handling, Foxconn is applying GR00T 2 to factory automation for server manufacturing and Siemens is evaluating it across industrial use cases. MicroAGI is using GR00T 2, post-trained through reinforcement learning, to perform Ethernet cable swapping with a YAM robotic arm. Its agentic robotics approach automates the creation and calibration of simulation environments using Isaac Lab 3.0 and Newton, where the policy is trained. The agentic robotics workflow will be demonstrated at CoRL. Training capable robots requires diverse data. Open NVIDIA workflows and models equip researchers with better tools for data collection and annotation: For researchers building robot-training datasets, NVIDIA’s new open Video to Data workflow turns human video into simulated robot demonstrations, with a challenge inviting researchers to advance it. The NVIDIA EgoHand open model — being demoed at CoRL and with over 40,000 Hugging Face downloads in the two weeks since launch — reconstructs 3D hand motion, trained with data from Noitom Robotics . https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/egohand-demo.mp4 Where the Training and Scaling Happens — in Simulation A pretrained model gives robots a core set of skills. Simulation lets researchers train, refine and evaluate skills at scale before deploying them on physical robots. NVIDIA Isaac Lab , an open source robot-learning framework, provides the foundation for that work. Its latest release, Isaac Lab 3.0 , allows researchers to use agents to quickly set up training environments with simulation-ready assets , switch between NVIDIA PhysX and Newton physics solvers , choose renderers for perception-based training and apply a new reinforcement post-training library to foundation models like GR00T. Accurate physics is critical to transferring learned skills from simulation to the real robot. Tighter integration with Newton , an open source physics engine, now allows Isaac Lab to model deformable objects such as cables and cloth, along with complex articulated systems such as robotic hands with many interacting joints. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/newton-strawberry.mp4 Integration with Newton simulates how a strawberry deforms under a robot’s grip. Together, Isaac Lab and Newton combine accurate physics with scale to enable researchers to train thousands of simulated robots in parallel. In a vision-based dexterous manipulation benchmark, Isaac Lab 3.0 with Newton achieved up to 2.5x the training throughput of Isaac Lab 2.3 with PhysX. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/newton-physx-web.mp4 Isaac Lab supports robot simulation with Newton and NVIDIA PhysX. Developers are extending Newton’s capabilities. At CoRL, Skild AI announced Scalable Throughput-optimized Engine for Embodied Learning, or STEEL, a new rigid-body physics solver built on Newton to accelerate robot training with Isaac Lab. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/robotics-montage-8s.mp4 Skild AI’s STEEL Solver. Flexion showcased how Isaac Lab and Newton help train Reflect, its robot-intelligence model combining reasoning and whole-body manipulation. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/flexion-newton-isaac-lab.mp4 Flexion uses Newton for RL with Isaac Lab. FieldAI is using Newton — as well as Isaac Lab and Isaac Sim, built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries — to train and validate robot policies for deployment in unstructured real-world environments. Dyna Robotics will demonstrate how parallel simulation in Isaac Lab helps train whole-body controllers for its semi-humanoid Taku robot for work in warehouses, hotels and food services. Walden Robotics is using Isaac Sim’s photorealistic rendering to train and evaluate its general-purpose robot in virtual environments for manufacturing and logistics, while Dexmate is exploring how coding agents can rehearse and refine manipulation strategies in Isaac Sim before executing them on its Vega robot. AlphaNIST , built in Isaac Lab, demonstrates how efficient practice can translate into precision. A single policy learns all 20 tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board, manipulating  millimeter-scale parts using only a yes-or-no success signal. It achieves more than 98% training success, compared with 81% for separate per-task policies, using roughly 39x less GPU time. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/alphanist-6-16s-web.mp4 AlphaNIST uses Isaac Lab to train a single robot policy across 20 precision tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board. Behind those results is Success-Guided Sampling , or SGS, from the University of Washington and NVIDIA. The method focuses practice on tasks a policy succeeds at about half the time, directing training toward skills it’s still learning. With SGS, robot training can scale beyond a million parallel environments. The University of Texas at Austin’s School of Computing and Texas Robotics uses Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to train robotic skills in simulation, letting students start developing before physical hardware is available. New Industrial Benchmarks for Robot Evaluation Learning a skill is one challenge. Performing it reliably across changing conditions is another. NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena , an open source framework for scaled policy evaluation, enables developers to compose diverse and repeatable evaluations, then run policies across thousands of variations in parallel. Analyses expose which conditions cause failures, so researchers know what to fix in their next training run. The developer preview of its latest version, 0.4, is arriving at CoRL. DexBench and VABAR, two new open benchmarks, are among the first designed to measure robot dexterity and adaptability across industrial tasks using Isaac Lab-Arena and Newton. DexBench , developed by RLWRLD in collaboration with NVIDIA, takes dexterity evaluation off the tabletop and into real-world workflows. Built using NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena, it features 15 tasks across four scenes spanning retail, logistics, manufacturing and hospitality, testing generalization across object, spatial and physics variations. Genesis AI , mimic robotics and other industry partners are evaluating DexBench through early access. Teams can run DexBench on Manifold, Bifrost’s evaluation platform for scaling robotics simulations, with no setup required, built-in failure analysis and free credits for initial evaluations. VABAR — the Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics — from UC Berkeley and NVIDIA, evaluates robots across six industrial tasks. Each carries standardized variations, difficulty tiers and success metrics. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/task-tool-sorting.mp4 A simulated tool-sorting task demonstrates how VABAR evaluates robot manipulation skills for industrial workflows. Agents Turn Skills Into Robot Programs Successful task completion requires robots to coordinate multiple skills and adapt when something goes wrong. Building reliable programs for these multistep tasks remains a challenge. Agentic robotics helps solve that challenge. UC Berkeley’s new Graph-as-Policy (GaP) framework uses agents to connect individual skills into robot programs. Agents test these programs using NVIDIA Isaac open simulation technologies and refine them based on failures. This helps researchers scale development with less data while keeping the programs interpretable for engineers to review and verify before deployment. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/wipe-the-bar.mp4 GaP uses agents and simulation to turn individual robot skills into coordinated actions, such as wiping a bar. “To me, agentic robotics is the most exciting technological development since the internet in 1995,” said Ken Goldberg, professor of robotics at UC Berkeley and a lead on the VABAR and GaP projects. Ambi Robotics is exploring GaP for industrial automation. Ambi Robotics , Bosch Research and Siemens are all exploring GaP for its agentic robotics workflows across diverse industrial scenarios. Learn more by joining NVIDIA at CoRL . title: Our newest TPUs: 8tx and 8i Max, built for the agentic era
body: Our newest TPUs: 8tx and 8i Max, built for the agentic era Nov 09, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link We’ve expanded our eighth generation TPU portfolio with TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, marking four new TPU systems in a single year. Amin Vahdat SVP and Chief Technologist, AI and Infrastructure Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Read AI-generated summary We’re expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with the new TPU 8tx for secure, confidential inference and TPU 8i Max for massive context windows. These systems help you manage complex agentic workloads by providing specialized hardware for security, density, and reasoning. You can learn more about these additions and our latest software updates by watching our broadcast or visiting the Google Cloud website to explore our full infrastructure lineup. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. We are expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with the new TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max systems. TPU 8tx provides hardware-level security for sensitive data, while TPU 8i Max handles massive context windows. These systems join TPU 8t and TPU 8i to offer specialized performance for every AI lifecycle stage. We are making TPUs more accessible by supporting PyTorch, open-source software, and automated tools for developers. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points We first designed TPUs more than a decade ago motivated by Google’s internal demands, including voice recognition and language translation. Eight generations of TPUs later, the use cases have exploded, covering: i) training and serving our own Gemini models, ii) agentic workloads, iii) delivering services to Google Cloud customers on our cloud infrastructure, and most recently, iv) allowing customers to deploy TPUs directly into their own data centers. TPUs are now a rapidly growing business with nearly 100 customers — including frontier labs, trading firms, retailers, universities, and more. At Google Cloud Next in April, we introduced two new specialized TPUs in the same generation — 8t for large-scale training and 8i for real-time reasoning. TPU 8t and 8i offer up to 2.7 times better training performance and 80% better inference price performance, respectively, versus our previous generation of TPUs. Today, we’re taking that a step further, expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with two additional systems: TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack, and TPU 8tx for secure and confidential inference. This is the first time we have introduced four TPU systems in a single year. Our expanded eighth-generation TPU portfolio: TPU 8t, TPU 8i, TPU 8tx, and TPU 8i Max. While we’ve always co-designed our TPUs in partnership with Google DeepMind, we’re now increasingly getting feedback from external organizations on their specific needs. With computing moving from human to agent scale, businesses are asking for accelerators that can reason across AI models’ massive context windows. In addition, some highly regulated customers are asking for specialized encryption capabilities for unique workloads. The new TPU systems we are announcing today address this new reality. Coupled with our recent PyTorch announcements , our aim is to make TPUs more easily accessible to every developer and Cloud customer. By combining modular custom silicon with an open and easy-to-use software stack, we can deliver new hardware and system configurations at the pace of the AI industry. Building the computer around the chip Today, we’re announcing two new TPU systems — and there’s an important difference between a new chip and a new system. Designing a new chip means laying out billions of microscopic transistors on a silicon wafer in a multi-year process bound by the laws of physics and a complex, long-duration manufacturing lifecycle. A system, on the other hand, is about how we bring together the compute, networking, and storage around the chip. This can include how they are packaged with the chips, to quickly meet emerging customer needs and research use cases. When we built our very first TPU more than a decade ago, we knew AI software would evolve much faster than silicon manufacturing ever could. So we made a foundational bet on system balance and modularity, architecting our TPUs as building blocks as part of our AI Hypercomputer , so engineers could rapidly adjust packaging, high-speed memory, optical networking, and security around them. That approach allows us to deliver specialized supercomputers in a matter of months rather than years. Specializing for secure, high-context AI Each system in our eighth-generation TPU portfolio targets a distinct part of the AI lifecycle. TPU 8t and TPU 8i established the baseline for this generation of chips: TPU 8t was designed to be a training powerhouse for massive foundation models with maximum “goodput” — or the useful intelligence delivered per watt of energy used. TPU 8i is the reasoning engine, designed to break the memory wall, cutting inter-chip communication delays by up to half. Now, as enterprises bring autonomous agents into production, we have created two new configurations of these foundational systems to solve two urgent new challenges: hardware-level data security and million-token context scale. TPU 8tx TPU 8tx, our third eighth-generation system, is optimized for secure and confidential inference and is also great for small-scale training. It’s built for regulated enterprises and governments running frontier or proprietary models and autonomous agents alongside their most sensitive data. Normally, data is encrypted when stored or sent over a network, but has to be unlocked in memory while a computer processes it. Built on the same silicon as TPU 8t and paired with 5th Generation AMD EPYC CPU hosts, TPU 8tx builds security directly into the hardware layer, keeping sensitive data and model weights protected and isolated even while in active use. And by adopting the same low-latency Boardfly network we created for real-time reasoning, TPU 8tx keeps multi-step agents moving, delivering up to 2x lower latency compared to TPU 8t with a near-zero performance penalty. Pairing training-grade compute with a fast inference network also means organizations can simultaneously run and customize their models on a single system. TPU 8tx enables teams to fine-tune models using their private data, distill large models into smaller ones, and train their agents through reinforcement learning, all without needing to migrate sensitive data between separate clusters. Designed for sensitive enterprise workloads, TPU 8tx provides hardware-level confidential compute for private fine-tuning and secure agent execution. TPU 8i Max Our fourth system, TPU 8i Max, is built for a different problem: the memory wall. When dozens of AI agents work together across an entire software codebase or hours of video at once, memory bandwidth quickly becomes the bottleneck. So we took two low-latency TPU 8i chips and combined them onto a single package. TPU 8i Max scales compute and memory in lockstep, delivering double the compute, double the SRAM and double the HBM bandwidth of TPU 8i, so processors remain equipped with essential data and so that large workloads do not stall. Further, because TPU 8i Max fits twice the silicon within the existing rack footprint, data centers can deploy significantly more computing power per square foot and per watt. The dual-chip TPU 8i Max system, engineered for massive context windows and maximum compute density. While flexible across workloads, together the four systems in our eighth-generation TPUs give customers a purpose-built accelerator for every stage of the agentic lifecycle. TPU 8t for scale-up training, TPU 8i for low-latency reasoning, TPU 8tx for confidential computing, and TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack. Opening up TPUs to every developer When we launched the first TPU more than a decade ago, there were only a handful of companies running workloads that needed the processing power of a TPU. The use cases were specialized, so engineers would use optimized frameworks and hand-tuned code. Over the years, as AI has advanced, more and more companies began using accelerators. Now, AI adoption is at a point where TPUs are excellent for a wide range of companies and use cases, and as a result, we’ve been working systematically to remove barriers to adoption so that TPUs are as easy-to-use as general-purpose hardware. This investment comes together today across these key areas: Opening up TPU development to every PyTorch developer; no code rewrites needed: Last month, we open-sourced TorchTPU , so PyTorch code and Hugging Face models now run natively on TPUs, alongside out-of-the-box TPU backends for leading open-source inference engines like vLLM and SGLang. And to make hardware optimization effortless, our new open-source TPU agent suite (now in preview) plugs directly into coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Google Antigravity to automate TPU onboarding in minutes, diagnose bottlenecks, and autotune custom kernels using plain language. For production deployments, our new open-source XLA Serving Engine lets you train models in Python and serve them directly in a low-latency C++ runtime across TPUs, GPUs, and CPUs. Industry-leading production performance on InferenceX and AgentX benchmarks: In production, what really matters is outcomes on real AI workloads rather than theoretical peak chip speeds. On industry-standard InferenceX and AgentX benchmarks , which test realistic agentic coding and long-context work, our native vLLM-TorchTPU software stack on TPUs achieved state-of-the-art price-performance marks. New evaluations demonstrate these advantages extend across a wide range of frontier open models and open-source serving stacks while maintaining high model accuracy. Upcoming software optimizations on this same hardware will drive those results even further. Eliminating idle compute waste for autonomous agents: Because AI agents are stateful, they frequently pause for seconds or hours while waiting on a database lookup, an external software tool, or human feedback. To make our accelerators more power-efficient during those pauses, our new Agent Compute Engine software automatically suspends idle agent sessions and shifts working memory off the chip in milliseconds, cutting operational infrastructure costs. Breaking through the memory wall with the model-state layer (TPU Sync): Building the computer around the chip also means unifying memory, storage, and networking in software. As agents reason across million-token contexts and continuous reinforcement learning (RL) loops, memory quickly becomes the bottleneck. We’re open-sourcing TPU Sync , the model-state layer for TPU clusters. TPU Sync turns chip HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the data center network into a single, co-designed memory hierarchy — automatically tiering massive KV caches off the chip in milliseconds, streaming context across disaggregated prefill and decode nodes, and synchronizing RL weights to cut KV transfer latency and Time to First Token (TTFT) by more than 90%. Scaling distributed workloads across TPUs from a single controller: Now generally available on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Cloud Pathways brings the Google DeepMind runtime behind Gemini to every Google Cloud customer. Using a single-controller architecture and pathwaysutils , you can orchestrate large-scale TPU systems across multiple slices as if they were one local machine for pre-training, reinforcement learning, and multihost inference. Cloud Pathways keeps long-running jobs moving through hardware disruptions with colocated Python sidecars, sub-minute slice hot-swapping, and elastic resharding. Stitching custom TPU topologies on-demand with GKE dynamic slicing: Now generally available, GKE dynamic slicing decouples physical hardware provisioning from logical slice formation using optical circuit switching (OCS) technology. By dynamically assembling TPU cubes into larger topologies (super-slicing) or partitioning them into smaller, isolated workloads (sub-slicing) on-the-fly, this update completely eliminates rigid, manual nodepool recreation cycles. This topology agility slashes job startup times by up to 5x and accelerates fault recovery by up to 4.5x, maximizing overall fleet utilization and workload goodput across all TPUs. Co-designing with a decade of experience Shipping four TPU systems and a unified, open software stack in a single year only happens when silicon architects, networking engineers, compiler teams, and Google DeepMind researchers build side-by-side. Increasingly, we’re even tapping into AI to ideate and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. From using Google DeepMind’s AlphaChip reinforcement learning system to using Gemini to deliver chip layouts in hours rather than weeks, we’re using TPU-powered AI services to rapidly accelerate next-generation TPU hardware development. This is true co-design and a unique Google differentiator. Learn more about our new TPU systems by tuning into today’s broadcast at 9 a.m. PT. title: Sex Offender Sentenced to Prison for Violating the Federal Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act
body: Press Release Sex Offender Sentenced to Prison for Violating the Federal Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of West Virginia CHARLESTON, W.Va. – Cory Alan Kinsel, also known as “Cory Alan Hatcher,” 38, was sentenced today to one year and two months in prison, to be followed by five years of supervised release, with the first six months of release to be served at a halfway house, for failing to register and update his registration as a sex offender as required by the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act (SORNA) after relocating from West Virginia to Ohio and obtaining employment in Kentucky. According to court documents and statements made in court,  on February 2, 2025, a law enforcement officer conducting a compliance check on Kinsel determined that Kinsel had left his registered address, a Charleston men’s shelter, without updating his registration. The resulting investigation revealed that Kinsel was living in South Point, Ohio, and working at a restaurant in Ashland, Kentucky, where he was arrested on October 8, 2025. Kinsel knew he was required to register as a sex offender and maintain that registration as a result of his conviction for third-degree sexual assault of a 13-year-old girl in Hancock County Circuit Court in 2007. United States Attorney Moore Capito made the announcement and commended the investigative work of the West Virginia State Police and the United States Marshals Service (USMS). United States District Judge Joseph R. Goodwin imposed the sentence. Assistant United States Attorney Jonathan T. Storage prosecuted the case. SORNA is part of the Adam Walsh Child Protection and Safety Act of 2006 and provides a comprehensive set of minimum standards for sex offender registration and notification in the United States. SORNA seeks to strengthen the nationwide network of sex offender registration and notification programs, in part by requiring registered sex offenders to register and keep their registration current in each jurisdiction in which they reside, work, or go to school. A copy of this press release is located on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia. Related court documents and information can be found on PACER by searching for Case No. 2:25-cr-179. ### Updated November 9, 2026 Component USAO - West Virginia, Southern

title: Merced County teacher indicted for distribution of child sexual abuse material (CSAM)
body: Press Release Merced County teacher indicted for distribution of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of California FRESNO, Calif. — On Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, a federal grand jury returned a two-count indictment against Patrick Silva, 38, of Hilmar, charging him with distribution of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and possession of CSAM, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. According to court documents, from November 2024 to September 2025, Silva used the internet to distribute CSAM. During the same period, Silva was a teacher at the Delhi High School in Merced. Homeland Security Investigations, the Central Valley Internet Crimes Against Children Taskforce, and the Merced County Sheriff’s Office conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Luke Baty is prosecuting the case. Silva pleaded not guilty today at his arraignment. He was arrested last Friday and remains in federal custody. A detention hearing is scheduled for Nov. 12, 2026. If convicted, Silva faces a maximum statutory penalty of 30 years in prison and a $250,000 fine. Any sentence, however, would be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute those who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc. Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - California, Eastern

title: Pecos Woman Pleads Guilty to IRS Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Pecos Woman Pleads Guilty to IRS Fraud Scheme Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A Pecos woman pleaded guilty to impersonating an IRS agent in order to defraud a victim out of more than $150,000. In her plea agreement, Sandra Vega , 48, admitted that between 2018 and March 2026, she posed as an Internal Revenue Agent in order to defraud John Doe by convincing him that he would receive a large sum of money from the IRS if he first paid a variety of fees and deposits totaling at least $150,000. The victim provided Vega with money with the expectation that Vega would transmit the money to the IRS. Vega did not send any of the victim’s money to the IRS. Instead, Vega spent all of the victim’s money on personal expenses. Vega pleaded guilty to five counts, including four counts of wire fraud and one count of false impersonation of a federal employee. At sentencing, Vega faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and restitution to the victim in an amount determined by the court. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison, Acting Special Agent in Charge Scott Brown of IRS Criminal Investigation's Phoenix Field Office and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today. The FBI Albuquerque Field Office and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation investigated this case with the assistance of the Bernalillo County Sheriff’s Office and Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration. The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of New Mexico is prosecuting the case. Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Fraud Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - New Mexico Press Release Number: 26-315

title: Gates County Repeat Offender Convicted on Child Porn Charges
body: Press Release Gates County Repeat Offender Convicted on Child Porn Charges Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of North Carolina USANCE.PublicInfoOfficer@usdoj.gov NEW BERN, N.C. – A federal jury convicted Myron Curtis Pelech, 46, of Gates County, also known as “Ping Pelech,” of transporting and possessing child porn. “This habitual pervert will no longer feed his disgusting fetishes hurting vulnerable children to stoke his twisted self-gratification. We will not tolerate this type of depraved behavior here,” said U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle. “This spider will only spin his web behind cold steel bars.” At the time of his arrest, Pelech was already on federal supervised release following a prior conviction in the Eastern District of North Carolina for receiving child porn in 2016. He had only been out of prison for less than a year before agents caught him engaging in this new similar criminal conduct. FBI agents arrested Pelech after tracing a significant volume of child sexual abuse material shared over the BitTorrent network to his room at the Regency Inn in Fayetteville. The BitTorrent Network is a decentralized system for sharing files across the internet. Instead of downloading a file from one central server, BitTorrent lets many users share pieces of the file with each other at the same time and in this case, child porn. When agents executed a search warrant at his room, they recovered a concealed cell phone and tablet hidden under the television stand. A forensic review of the cell phone revealed that Pelech had saved a screenshot of a website dedicated to child sexual exploitation. Agents unlocked the tablet and located more than 150 videos and over 200 images of child sexual abuse material. The files depicted abhorrent severe exploitation of very young children. Pelech faces a federal prison sentence of 15 to 40 years for transporting child pornography and 10 to 20 years for possessing child pornography. Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina made the announcement after U.S. District Judge Louise W. Flanagan accepted the verdict. The FBI is investigating the case. A copy of this press release is located on our website . Related court documents and information can be found on the website of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina or on PACER by searching for Case No. 7:22-CR-367-FL. Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Operation Take Back America Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - North Carolina, Eastern

title: Lebanon Man Sentenced to 25 Years for Sexual Exploitation of a Minor
body: Press Release Lebanon Man Sentenced to 25 Years for Sexual Exploitation of a Minor Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Indiana INDIANAPOLIS- Erick Christian, 50, of Lebanon, Indiana, has been sentenced to 25 years in federal prison, followed by 15 years of supervised release, after pleading guilty to two counts of sexual exploitation of a child. Christian was also ordered to pay $3,000 in restitution to the minor victim. According to court documents, on October 19, 2023, law enforcement received information from the Indiana Department of Child Services that a minor female, Minor Victim 1, had been sexually molested by a family member identified as Erick Christian. When interviewed, Minor Victim 1 stated that the sexual abuse, which included frequent oral intercourse, began when she was approximately six years old and lasted until she was approximately eleven years old. Christian took sexually explicit photos of the child during the abuse, while she was showering, and forced her to wear adult lingerie. On March 14, 2025, law enforcement executed a search warrant at Christian’s home and found a cell phone containing sexually explicit photos of MV1, as well as at least 320 images depicting minors or computer-generated minors engaged in sexually explicit conduct. The ages of those minors ranged from toddlers to teenagers. “Especially horrific are predators who abuse children in a place meant to be a safe-haven—their home. The defendant stripped his victim from the safety and security that she should have been entitled to and turned that home into a house of horrors, where she was subjected to sexual abuse over the course of many years,” said Tom Wheeler, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Indiana. “The pursuit of those who victimize children is some of the most important work our office does, and Erick Christian will spend decades in prison thanks to the dedication and commitment of our law enforcement partners and our AUSAs.” “A child’s home should be a place of safety, not a place where she is sexually abused and exploited by someone she should be able to trust. This defendant robbed a young girl of that security, repeatedly victimizing her over the course of years and documenting his abuse,” said FBI Indianapolis Special Agent in Charge Timothy J. O’Malley. “His 25-year prison sentence sends a clear message: those who prey on children will be relentlessly pursued and held accountable. The FBI remains committed to protecting children and bringing those who exploit them to justice.” The Federal Bureau of Investigation, Indianapolis Division and the Lebanon Police Department investigated this case. The sentence was imposed by U.S. District Judge Sarah Evans Barker. U.S. Attorney Wheeler thanked Assistant U.S. Attorneys, Carolyn Haney and MaryAnn T. Mindrum, who prosecuted this case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood , a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. If you are a victim of child sexual exploitation, please contact your local police department. Resources for victims of child exploitation can be found on our website at https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdin/project-safe-childhood ### Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Indiana, Southern

title: New Orleans Man Guilty of Federal Fentanyl and Firearm Charges
body: Press Release New Orleans Man Guilty of Federal Fentanyl and Firearm Charges Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – JOSHUA BENSON (“ BENSON ”), a/k/a “Big Mal,” age 36, of New Orleans, pled guilty on November 3, 2026, before United States District Judge Wendy B. Vitter to Counts One, Three, Four, Five, and Six of a six-count indictment charging him with violations of the Federal Controlled Substances and Gun Control Acts, announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. BENSON pled guilty to Count One, possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl, in violation of Title 21, United States Code, Sections 841(a)(1) and 841(b)(1)(A). In Count Three, BENSON pled guilty to being a felon in possession of a firearm, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 922(g)(1) and 924(a)(8). BENSON also pled guilty to Counts Four, Five, and Six, distribution of fentanyl, in violation of Title 21, United States Code, Sections 841(a)(1), 841(b)(1)(B), and 841(b)(1)(C). As to the fentanyl possession charge in Count One, BENSON faces a mandatory minimum sentence of ten years up to life imprisonment, up to a $10,000,000 fine, and at least five years of supervised release. As to the felon in possession charge in Count Three, BENSON faces up to fifteen years in prison, up to a $250,000 fine, and up to three years of supervised release. As to the fentanyl distribution charge in Count Four, BENSON faces a mandatory minimum sentence of five years up to forty years in prison, up to a $5,000,000 fine, and at least four years of supervised release. As to each fentanyl distribution charge in Counts Five and Six, BENSON faces up to twenty years in prison, up to a $1,000,000 fine, and at least three years of supervised release. Each count also carries a mandatory special assessment fee of $100. According to court documents, between August and October 2025, BENSON sold nearly 100 grams of fentanyl to a confidential informant working with the Drug Enforcement Administration, in three controlled purchases near his residence in New Orleans. On October 30, 2025, agents executed federal search warrants at BENSON ’s apartment and a second residence. In BENSON ’s apartment, agents found more than one kilogram of fentanyl, much of it hidden behind the headboard of his bed, along with a digital scale, a vacuum sealer, and $5,080 in cash. In a storage drawer built into BENSON ’s bed, agents found a loaded Heckler & Koch nine-millimeter pistol fitted with an extended magazine. At the second residence, agents seized a safe holding $48,000 in cash. BENSON is prohibited from possessing firearms because of a prior felony conviction for attempted armed robbery with a firearm. Sentencing is set for February 2, 2027, before United States District Judge Wendy B. Vitter. U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and the New Orleans Police Department. Assistant United States Attorneys Paul J. Hubbell, IV and Briana Williams of the Narcotics Unit; and Narcotics Unit Supervisor Lynn Schiffman are in charge of the prosecution. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . *** Contact Shane M. title: Justice Department Awards Jackson, Mississippi, more than $63M to Combat Violent Crime and Restore Law and Order Through Model Cities Initiative
body: Press Release Justice Department Awards Jackson, Mississippi, more than $63M to Combat Violent Crime and Restore Law and Order Through Model Cities Initiative Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Jackson Was Selected Out of Nearly 50 American Cities to Receive Federal Funding to Strengthen Law Enforcement and Enhance Public Safety. Today, the Justice Department awarded Jackson, Mississippi, more than $63 million through its Model Cities Initiative (MCI), a flagship effort to reduce violent crime, restore law and order, and strengthen public safety in communities across the country. “The Model Cities Initiative reflects the Trump Administration’s commitment to reducing crime across the country and ensuring the safety of every American,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “These cities are setting an example of proactive law enforcement that will strengthen the rule of law and improve public safety in their jurisdictions. As violent crime rates continue to fall to historic lows, the Department of Justice is redoubling our efforts to invest in local communities and keep American families safe.” “Jackson has made real progress against violent crime, and that progress deserves recognition,” said U.S. Marshals Service Director Gadyaces S. Serralta. “The officers working these cases know their city and understand the challenges ahead.  This investment gives them an opportunity to build on the work they’ve already done, with better tools to investigate violent crime and bring those responsible before the courts.  The goal is simple: give good officers every advantage against violent crime.” “This is a tremendous win for Jackson and Mississippi. I’m grateful to President Trump and Attorney General Blanche for partnering with us to make our capital city a safer place,” said Governor Tate Reeves of Mississippi. “Since day one, we’ve made enhancing public safety a top priority. We’ve invested in law enforcement, put more officers on the streets and held criminals accountable. This investment will provide additional resources to combat crime and help protect the people of this amazing city.” “With this significant investment, the Trump Administration is demonstrating a commitment to the people of Jackson to help reduce criminal activity, restore law and order, and positively impact the quality of life for Jacksonians,” said Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch. “We are proud to be a partner with the City of Jackson and all our local, state, and federal partners in this effort to make Mississippi’s capital city stronger, safer, and more secure. A strong Jackson means a strong Mississippi.” “This investment gives Jackson more resources to strengthen public safety and support the people who protect our city every day,” said Mayor John Horhn. “I thank the Department of Justice for its support and our congressional delegation and state leaders for helping us get here. Funding is essential, but making Jackson safer takes all of us — faith leaders, neighborhood associations, educators, businesses, and neighbors working together. We want every family to be able to raise their children, pursue opportunities, and enjoy life in Jackson without fear.” “True public safety requires us to address not only crime, but also the conditions that contribute to it. The MCI Grant provides an opportunity to strengthen our forensic capabilities, technology, and invest in the people who serve this community,” said Chief of Police Dr. RaShall M. Brackney. “These investments are essential to building a police department that is not only better equipped to investigate and prevent crime, but also better positioned to address the complex challenges that shaped public safety in Jackson.” Image of Attorney General Todd Blanche at the Model Cities Initiative in Jackson, Mississippi Image of $63 Million Check Awarded to City of Jackson Jackson, Mississippi, was selected in large part because of its substantial progress in reducing violent crime. The city has cut annual homicides by more than half, from 156 in 2021 to 75 in 2025. While these gains are significant, Jackson continues to face persistent challenges related to gun violence, investigative capacity, and public safety infrastructure. Through the Model Cities Initiative, the city seeks to build on its recent successes by strengthening law enforcement capabilities, expanding intelligence-driven investigations, and enhancing coordination among local, state, and federal public safety partners. Jackson's proposal includes transforming its existing Real-Time Command Center into a comprehensive Real-Time Public Safety Center, modernizing forensic and ballistic analysis capabilities, and establishing a specialized unit to integrate ballistic evidence and criminal intelligence with targeted enforcement strategies. The city also plans to deploy a Sky-to-Street Public Safety Network utilizing unmanned aircraft systems to improve situational awareness, accelerate emergency response, and support crime reduction efforts. Additional priorities include expanding law enforcement staffing, strengthening services for crime victims, and enhancing behavioral health and community reentry programs. Collectively, these investments are designed to reduce violent crime, improve investigative outcomes, and create a sustainable, coordinated framework for public safety in Jackson. The MCI takes a whole-of-city approach to public safety, bringing together law enforcement agencies, local government officials, and community partners to develop comprehensive strategies that address the unique public safety challenges facing their communities. The applications submitted by the four selected jurisdictions exemplified the innovative, forward-thinking approaches the Department sought through the initiative. While each jurisdiction faces unique public safety challenges and brings different priorities, resources, and starting points to the initiative, the Department is confident in the strength of their proposals and their commitment to achieving meaningful results. Despite differing approaches, all four jurisdictions demonstrated a shared determination to reduce violent crime and make their communities safer. Through the initiative, the Justice Department will work with each jurisdiction to finalize and implement its public safety plan. Funding will support a range of priorities, including hiring sworn and non-sworn law enforcement officers and other personnel to support enforcement, prosecution, and related public safety activities; adopting new and improved technology; purchasing or leasing equipment; enhancing forensic capabilities and capacity; and providing services to address mental health and substance use issues and reduce recidivism. The Justice Department announced the Model Cities Initiative in June 2026 to build on early successes in jurisdictions such as Memphis, Tennessee, and Washington, D.C., in reducing violence, crime, and disorder. The initiative directs nearly $300 million in federal resources toward comprehensive public safety strategies that strengthen law enforcement, improve coordination among public safety partners, and address the factors contributing to crime and recidivism. Through these investments, the Justice Department will work alongside local partners to implement sustainable public safety solutions and deliver measurable results. The four Model Cities will help advance the Administration’s efforts to reject the status quo of allowing crime and disorder to go unchecked and restore law, order, and safety to communities across the nation. Jacksonville, Florida; Baton Rouge, Louisiana; and St. Louis, Missouri, have additionally been selected to receive federal investments supporting innovative, comprehensive, locally driven strategies to combat crime and enhance coordination among federal, state, and local law enforcement partners. The specific departments funded are: Baton Rouge - East Baton Rouge Parish, Louisiana; Jackson - City of Jackson, Mississippi; Jacksonville - City of Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office; and St. Louis - City of St. Louis Police Department. Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component Office of the Attorney General Press Release Number: 26-1334

title: Pensacola Felon Indicted on Federal Firearm Charge
body: Press Release Pensacola Felon Indicted on Federal Firearm Charge Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Pensacola, Florida – Jeremy Olds, 39, of Pensacola, Florida, has been indicted in federal court for possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida, announced the charge. Olds appeared before U.S. Magistrate Judge Hope T. Cannon for his arraignment at the United States Courthouse in Pensacola, Florida. Trial is set for December 14, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. before U.S. District Judge M. Casey Rodgers. If convicted, Olds faces up to 15 years in prison, three years of supervised release, and a $250,000 fine. The case is being investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Brooke D. Lindsay. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . An indictment is merely an allegation by a grand jury that a defendant has committed a violation of federal criminal law; it is not evidence of guilt. All defendants are presumed innocent and entitled to a fair trial, during which the government bears the burden of proving guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website.  For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . title: Man Sentenced to 14 Years for Attempting to Coerce a 15-year-old to Engage in Prostitution
body: Press Release Man Sentenced to 14 Years for Attempting to Coerce a 15-year-old to Engage in Prostitution Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California Kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO – K’John Henry Sands II of Los Angeles was sentenced in federal court today to 168 months in prison for attempting to coerce a 15-year-old minor to engage in prostitution. Sands pleaded guilty on August 25, 2026, to one count of Attempted Coercion and Enticement of a Minor. According to his plea agreement, Sands also admitted to video recording the minor performing oral sex on him. As a part of his scheme, Sands instructed the minor regarding how much to charge for commercial sex dates, supplied the minor with condoms for the dates, and then collected the proceeds. Sands’ conduct came to the attention of the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force when, on June 2, 2025, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children sent information about an active MegaPersonals ad for what appeared to be a juvenile in the San Diego area. On June 3, 2025, investigators arranged a ruse commercial sex date and recovered the minor. Investigators then learned that the motel room in which the minor was staying had been rented by Sands. “Those who prey on vulnerable children should know that law enforcement will pursue justice relentlessly,” said U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon. “This sentence proves that combating the trafficking and exploitation of children remains an utmost priority at the California Department of Justice,” said California Attorney General Rob Bonta. “Crimes against children will never be tolerated in California, and together, we remain dedicated to holding perpetrators of child exploitation accountable. I am grateful for the hard work of my team in the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force that made securing this prison sentence possible." “This case reflects the strength of the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force and its partner agencies, whose swift, coordinated, and victim-centered response helped safeguard a vulnerable child and bring the offender to justice,” said Kevin Murphy, Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations San Diego. “HSI remains committed to working with our law enforcement and community partners to protect children and support survivors of trafficking.” In the government’s sentencing memo, prosecutors noted that the defendant was unconcerned with his victim’s age.“Mr. Sands’ intentions were clear: (The victim) was expected to make Mr. Sands money… It apparently did not matter that (she) was just 15 years old.” This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Derek Ko, with prior assistance from Assistant U.S. Attorney Lyndzie M. Carter. If you believe you or someone you know has been a victim of human trafficking, investigators ask that you contact the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force at 1-888-373-7888 or text 233733. DEFENDANT Case Number 25cr03258-BJC K’John Henry Sands II                                    Age: 26                         Los Angeles, CA SUMMARY OF CHARGES Attempted Coercion and Enticement of a Minor, 18 U.S.C., Section 2422 Maximum penalty: Life imprisonment with a 10-year mandatory minimum; $250,000 fine INVESTIGATING AGENCIES San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force San Diego Sheriff’s Office Homeland Security Investigations The San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force is a cooperative effort involving the California Department of Justice, California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, California Highway Patrol, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations, National City Police Department, Naval Criminal Investigative Service, San Diego City Attorney’s Office, San Diego County District Attorney’s Office, San Diego County Probation Department, San Diego County Sheriff’s Department, Chula Vista Police Department, San Diego Police Department, Southwest Border High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California. This case is the result of the ongoing efforts of the Special Victims Unit.  Formed in April 2025, the SVU is tasked with leading collaborations between federal and local law enforcement in the investigation and prosecution of cases involving sex trafficking and child exploitation, civil rights, and labor trafficking. The SVU oversees the Southern District of California liaisons to the San Diego Human Trafficking Task Force and Project Safe Childhood Contact Kelly Thornton, Director of Media Relations Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Human Trafficking Component USAO - California, Southern Press Release Number: CAS26-1109-Sands

title: Justice Department Sues the City of Glendale, California for Violating Citizens’ Second Amendment Rights Through Unreasonable Fees and Processes for Legal Firearm Permitting
body: Press Release Justice Department Sues the City of Glendale, California for Violating Citizens’ Second Amendment Rights Through Unreasonable Fees and Processes for Legal Firearm Permitting Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Today, the United States Department of Justice sued the City of Glendale, California, for violating citizens’ fundamental rights under the Second Amendment by requiring unreasonable fees to obtain concealed carry permits. “The Department of Justice is committed to protecting law abiding citizens’ right to keep and bear arms under the Second Amendment,” said Acting Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Jesus Osete. “The City of Glendale cannot impose unreasonable fees and unbridled discretion that undermines that core constitutional right.” “The right to bear arms is a fundamental right the Founding Fathers enshrined during our republic’s earliest years,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. “Exorbitant government fees that interfere with this right are abhorrent to our Constitution and our nation’s founding principles. This Justice Department will not stand by and watch our freedoms be eroded.” The Glendale Police Department (Glendale PD) administers a permitting regime with a total cost of an initial application for a concealed carry permit ranging from $1,971.00 to $2,106.00. The total cost for a renewal application, which citizens must complete every two years, is $1,271.00 to $1,406.00. These exorbitant amounts are a stark contrast to costs from the previous fiscal year when Glendale PD required only a $100 fee for first-time applicants and a $25 fee for renewals. Glendale PD also requires applicant reference interviews, psychological exams, interviews of the applicant, and a review of public statements including social media. Glendale PD does not publish any objective standards that they apply to these checks. It is well established that concealed carrying is a right. New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass’n, Inc. v. Bruen , 597 U.S. 1, 38 n. 9, 70 (2022). Glendale PD’s permitting fees are an unreasonable barrier to exercising that right, and its permitting regime lacks the “narrow, objective, and definite standards” which Bruen requires. Glendale PD’s policies and practices, therefore, violate the fundamental rights to keep and bear lawful firearms. The Second Amendment Section of the Civil Rights Division enforces the Second Amendment , the Police Pattern or Practice Act ( 34 U.S.C. § 12601 ), and Executive Order 14206 . If you are a current or prospective gun owner and believe that a state or local government has infringed your right to keep and bear arms, please submit a complaint through www.justice.gov/crt/second-amendment-section. Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Civil Rights Component Civil Rights Division Press Release Number: 26-1337
