title: Justice Department Sues Lyft for Denying Rides to Passengers with Service Dogs, Wheelchairs
body: Press Release Justice Department Sues Lyft for Denying Rides to Passengers with Service Dogs, Wheelchairs Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Today, the Justice Department (Department) filed a lawsuit against Lyft Inc., for discriminating against passengers with disabilities, including those who use service animals and mobility devices such as stowable wheelchairs. Lyft provides an important transportation option for millions of people throughout the United States. The lawsuit seeks $53 million for individuals with disabilities who Lyft has discriminated against, and who have submitted complaints to Lyft or the Department. “Individuals with disabilities should be able to rely on rideshare services free of discrimination,” said Acting Assistant Attorney General Jesus A. Osete of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “We intend to uphold the ADA’s promise that people with disabilities are entitled to equal access in every part of public life, including essential transportation services.” “Our purpose in the Department of Justice is often to fight for what’s right on behalf of those who can’t fight for themselves. And there are few areas where the fight is more important than in ensuring equal access to transportation services for all Americans,” said U.S Attorney Craig H. Missakian for the Northern District of California. “We take these allegations of misconduct seriously and, like our case against Uber for similar discriminatory conduct, we will devote all the resources necessary to make things right. The stakes are high and we owe those with disabilities nothing less.” The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, alleges Lyft violated Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA), which prohibits private transportation companies, such as Lyft, from discriminating based on disability. The ADA requires Lyft to transport individuals with disabilities and their service animals, and to provide rides and assist riders with stowable wheelchairs and mobility devices. A service animal is a dog trained to perform a task related to a person’s disability. Under the ADA, emotional support dogs are not service animals because providing emotional support is not a task related to a person’s disability. The Department’s civil complaint alleges that Lyft and its drivers routinely refuse service to individuals with disabilities; impose impermissible surcharges by charging fees such as cancellation fees to riders whom Lyft has unlawfully denied service; and refuse to reasonably modify Lyft’s policies, practices, or procedures where necessary to avoid discriminating against riders with disabilities, including by denying individuals with mobility disabilities the option to sit in the front seat when needed. The lawsuit seeks a court order to force Lyft to stop discriminating against individuals with disabilities, to modify its policies to comply with the ADA, and to train its staff and drivers on the ADA.  In addition to the monetary damages to compensate aggrieved individuals subjected to Lyft’s discrimination, the lawsuit demands that Lyft pay a civil penalty to vindicate the public’s interest in eliminating disability discrimination. To learn more about the Civil Rights Division visit www.justice.gov/crt , and to report possible violations of federal civil rights laws go to www.civilrights.justice.gov . For more information on the ADA, please call the department’s toll-free ADA Information Line at 800-514-0301 (TTY 1-833-610-1264) or visit www.ada.gov . Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Civil Rights Component Civil Rights Division Press Release Number: 26-1338

title: Chinese National Charged with Attempted Sex Trafficking of a 15-Year-Old Girl
body: Press Release Chinese National Charged with Attempted Sex Trafficking of a 15-Year-Old Girl Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Florida MIAMI – A Chinese national has been charged with attempting to sex traffic a 15-year-old girl. According to court records, Dexing Zhang, 40, residing in Naples, communicated by phone and messaging application with a person he believed to be the mother of a 15-year-old girl and discussed arranging a sexual encounter with the minor in Davie. Zhang allegedly offered to pay $300 to engage in a sex act with the purported minor. He was arrested at a hotel after driving from Naples to meet the girl for the planned encounter. Zhang is charged with attempted sex trafficking of a minor. If convicted, Zhang faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years in federal prison and a maximum penalty of life in prison. Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas for the Southern District of Florida and Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement. FBI Miami is investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jodi Anton is prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorney’s Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate better, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov . To report suspected human trafficking or to obtain resources for victims, please call 1-888-373-7888; text “BeFree” (233733), or live chat at HumanTraffickingHotline.org . The toll-free phone, SMS text lines, and online chat function are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. Help is available in English, Spanish, Creole, or in more than 200 additional languages. The National Hotline is not managed by law enforcement, immigration, or an investigative agency. Correspondence with the National Hotline is confidential, and you may request assistance or report a tip anonymously. To report online child sexual exploitation, visit https://report.cybertip.org/ or call 1-800-843-5678. The Cyber Tip Line is operated by the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) in partnership with HSI and other law enforcement agencies. To learn more about the National Resource Hotline, visit www.humantraffickinghotline.org . To learn more about the U.S. Department of Justice’s efforts to combat human trafficking, visit www.justice.gov/humantrafficking . Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case number 26-cr-60254. ### Contact Public Affairs Unit U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of Florida USAFLS.News@usdoj.gov Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Florida, Southern

title: OPERATION TAKE BACK AMERICA: Previously Removed Illegal Alien Sentenced to Prison for Immigration and Firearm Offenses
body: Press Release OPERATION TAKE BACK AMERICA: Previously Removed Illegal Alien Sentenced to Prison for Immigration and Firearm Offenses Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Alabama OPERATION TAKE BACK AMERICA BIRMINGHAM, Ala. –  An illegal alien has been sentenced for immigration and firearm offenses, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr. U.S. District Court Judge Anna M. Manasco sentenced Federico Sanchez Alvarado (Sanchez), 29, a citizen of Mexico, to 21 months in prison. Sanchez pleaded guilty to illegal reentry after deportation/removal and illegal alien in possession of a firearm. According to the plea agreement, Sanchez was ordered removed from the United States on February 10, 2016, and deported on August 16, 2016. Sanchez came to law enforcement’s attention again when officers with the Pelham Police Department responded to a 911 call on October 17, 2025, for “shots fired.” Upon arrival, the officers heard a series of gun shots in a residential area behind Deer Springs Road.  Sanchez admitted to shooting a pistol in the backyard and agreed to show officers where his gun was located inside the residence.  Officers recovered from inside the residence a Springfield Armory XD-9 sub-compact handgun, which had been reported stolen two weeks earlier in Birmingham, Alabama. After having been found illegally in the United States a second time, Sanchez was arrested. “This sentence sends a clear message that those who disregard our immigration and firearms laws will be held accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. “We appreciate the work of our law enforcement partners on this case. Through our strong partnerships, we will continue working together to keep our communities safe. This case is another indication of how our nation’s immigration laws have been flaunted and abused. This individual is on his second deportation, but the Department of Justice will diligently continue to enforce the laws that secure our borders.” “Illegal aliens who disregard our laws, in this case by reentering the country after being removed and illegally possessing a firearm, pose a serious risk to the community,” said Ellen Johnson, Acting Special Agent in Charge of HSI in Georgia and Alabama. “HSI will continue working alongside our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners to identify and investigate individuals who threaten public safety and hold them accountable for their actions.” This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Homeland Security Investigations investigated the case along with Pelham Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Scott Woodard prosecuted the case. title: Wood County Man Sentenced to Prison for $510,465.19 Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Wood County Man Sentenced to Prison for $510,465.19 Fraud Scheme Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of West Virginia CHARLESTON, W.Va. – Jeffrey Jeffers, 35, of Williamstown, was sentenced today to two years and six months in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered to pay $510,465.19 in restitution for wire fraud. Jeffers admitted to stealing $510,465.19 from his employer through false charges to company-issued credit cards. According to court documents and statements made in court, between November 2022 and July 2024, Jeffers delivered products by truck for a large provider of industrial gas from its distribution facility in Wood County. The delivery trucks were fueled at the distribution facility and were also equipped with fuel credit cards. As part of his guilty plea, Jeffers admitted that he fraudulently charged a total of $510,465.19 to the fuel credit cards throughout his term of employment. Jeffers admitted that he opened online payment platform accounts in the names of fictitious service stations he created as part of his scheme. Jeffers charged more than 900 phantom fuel purchases to his employer’s fuel credit cards, payable to his fake service station accounts. Jeffers admitted that his delivery routes normally never required any refueling outside of the distribution facility. United States Attorney Moore Capito made the announcement and commended the investigative work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). United States District Judge Joseph R. Goodwin imposed the sentence. Assistant United States Attorney Gabriel Price prosecuted the case. A copy of this press release is located on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia. Related court documents and information can be found on PACER by searching for Case No. 2:26-cr-85. ### Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Fraud Component USAO - West Virginia, Southern

title: DEFENDANTS SENTENCED TO FEDERAL PRISON FOR CONSPIRACY TO COMMIT THEFTS FROM ATMS
body: Press Release DEFENDANTS SENTENCED TO FEDERAL PRISON FOR CONSPIRACY TO COMMIT THEFTS FROM ATMS Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Louisiana Three defendants who resided in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and Houston, Texas, were recently sentenced to federal prison by U.S. District Judge Brian A. Jackson for conspiracy to commit bank burglary and bank theft. They previously pled guilty to their respective charges. Deantae D. Mason, age 26, of Baton Rouge, Louisiana, was sentenced to 24 months imprisonment, followed by a term of three years of supervised release, and was further ordered to pay $285,120 in restitution and forfeit $95,039.99. Alex A. Mata, age 23, of Houston, Texas, was sentenced to 22 months imprisonment, followed by a term of three years of supervised release, and was further ordered to pay $285,120 in restitution and forfeit $95,039.99. Brandon C. Griffin, Jr., age 26, of Houston, Texas, was sentenced to 12 months and 1 day imprisonment followed by a term of three years of supervised release and was further ordered to pay $106,120 in restitution and forfeit $35,373.33. According to admissions made as part of their guilty pleas, local law enforcement was alerted to numerous attempted and successful burglaries of ATMs in the Baton Rouge area. The incidents involved similar characteristics and modus operandi, including the use of stolen vehicles, typically large trucks, and tow straps to pull open ATM doors or completely remove them from their concrete base. Members of the conspiracy scouted banks for potential ATM thefts, surveilled nearby areas for large trucks to steal, and served as lookouts while other members committed the ATM burglaries. Specifically, an ATM at a Pelican State Credit Union branch located on N. Lobdell Boulevard in Baton Rouge was ripped from its concrete base and destroyed. Approximately $106,120 was taken from the bank. Mason, Griffin, and Mata admitted to participating in this incident. Subsequently, an ATM at a Neighbors Federal Credit Union branch on Howell Boulevard in Baton Rouge was also burglarized. Approximately $179,000 was taken and the bank suffered significant damage to its ATM. Mason and Mata admitted to participating in this incident, as well. U.S. Attorney Kurt L. Wall praised the work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Baton Rouge Police Department, and East Baton Rouge Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Stephen Vick and Will Morris, who also serves as Criminal Chief, led the prosecution. Updated November 9, 2026 Component USAO - Louisiana, Middle

title: Buffalo man sentenced for gun possession
body: Press Release Buffalo man sentenced for gun possession Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of New York BUFFALO, N.Y. – U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Nazir Binhuguley, 24, of Cheektowaga, NY, who was convicted of possession of a firearm in furtherance of drug trafficking, was sentenced to serve 60 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Richard J. Arcara. On May 6, 2025, law enforcement executed the search warrant at Binhuguley’s Trent Square apartment, which he utilized for his drug trafficking activities. During the search, investigators seized three firearms, ammunition, a high-capacity pistol magazine, drug paraphernalia, a quantity of suspected fentanyl, and approximately $2,165 in cash. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Buffalo comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigations, Department of Homeland Security Enforcement and Removal Operations, Customs and Border Protection, the Drug Enforcement Administration, the U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, the U.S. Marshals Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the U.S. Secret Service, and the Diplomatic Security Service, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of New York. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael J. Adler. title: Miramar Beach Man Forfeits Foreign Antiquities to United States
body: Press Release Miramar Beach Man Forfeits Foreign Antiquities to United States Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Pensacola, Florida – Matthew Weinberg, of Miramar Beach, Florida, forfeited to the United States multiple antiquities dating as far back as circa 3000 BC. The seizure and forfeiture was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Thanks to the hard work of my tenacious attorneys, these improperly obtained foreign antiquities have been recovered and will be repatriated back to their countries of origin. Special thanks go to our federal law enforcement partners for investigating these violations of our anti-smuggling statutes, and for ensuring these ancient artifacts are returned to their rightful owners.” Court documents reveal that in July 2025, agents from Homeland Security Investigations were notified by the U.S. Customs and Border Protection Office in Pensacola, Florida, regarding the detention of a shipment inbound to Pensacola International Airport from the United Arab Emirates. The shipment was detained but was destined for Weinberg. The manifest for the shipment claimed it contained two terracotta objects valued at less than $200 but, in truth, upon appraisal after detention, it contained two cuneiform tablets valued at over $15,000 in total that date back to 3000-2000 BC from modern day Iraq. Multiple other shipments to Weinberg were then investigated, and it was determined that he obtained shipments, contrary to law, from Iran, Egypt, and Cyprus as well. All of these shipments were significantly undervalued on their manifests just as were the tablets from Iraq. These shipments included bronze figures, ceramic architectural models, and terracotta idols. In March 2026, federal agents executed a search and seizure warrant on Weinberg’s residence in Miramar Beach. Seized from his residence were, amongst other things, ancient Hebrew Torah scrolls, scroll artwork originating from China, and items from circa 712-525 BC Egypt. Below are sample images of some of the items seized from Weinberg by the Department of Homeland Security: Due to import restrictions agreed upon by the United States and Iraq, Egypt, Cyprus, and other countries, Weinberg was prohibited from the possession of these artifacts. In addition to forfeiting the artifacts to the United States for repatriation back to their countries of origin, Weinberg forfeited $75,000 in United States currency as proceeds of violations of federal anti-smuggling statutes. He will also be barred for two years from selling or purchasing any foreign antiquities or artifacts. The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and U.S. Customs and Border Protection in Pensacola, Florida. The case was handled by Assistant United States Attorneys Winifred L. Acosta and David L. Goldberg. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General.  To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . Contact United States Attorney’s Office Northern District of Florida USAFLN.Press.Office@usdoj.gov X: @USAO_NDFL Updated November 9, 2026 Component USAO - Florida, Northern

title: Denver Man Sentenced To 89 Months After Pleading Guilty to Drug and Firearms Charges
body: Press Release Denver Man Sentenced To 89 Months After Pleading Guilty to Drug and Firearms Charges Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Colorado USACO.PublicAffairs@usdoj.gov DENVER – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Colorado announces that Christopher Epperson, 56, of Denver, was sentenced to 89 months in prison after pleading guilty to one count of possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and one count of being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition. According to the plea agreement and facts established at sentencing, between July and August 2025, Epperson, who was at the time an eight-time convicted felon with prior convictions for burglary, aggravated robbery, domestic assault, attempted discharge of an illegal firearm, and felony menacing with a real/simulated weapon, and currently on federal supervised release for a prior felon in possession of firearm and ammunition conviction, was seen by law enforcement selling drugs to multiple people. On August 13, 2025, when law enforcement tried to stop Epperson, he ran from police and, while he was running, threw a bag he was carrying on his person. Law enforcement retrieved and searched the bag and found 54.7 grams of fentanyl, 13.55 grams of cocaine base, and 102.5 grams of methamphetamine. Law enforcement also found other drug dealing paraphernalia and $9,106 in cash. Epperson was ultimately arrested and his car was subsequently searched. Inside the car, law enforcement found a loaded firearm. As part of his plea, Epperson admitted to possessing the fentanyl, meth, and cocaine base with the intent to sell them for human consumption. Epperson also admitted he possessed the loaded firearm to further his drug-trafficking activities. “The sentencing of this repeat offender is another step in our ongoing efforts to safeguard Colorado communities,” said United States Attorney for the District of Colorado Peter McNeilly. “We are committed to putting violent drug dealers behind bars.” “Fentanyl, methamphetamine, and cocaine continue to be trafficked and distributed in our region, and these illegal drugs continue to destroy lives and ruin communities,” said Drug Enforcement Administration Rocky Mountain Field Division Special Agent in Charge Mark Putnam. “Our thanks to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Colorado, and our other investigative partners in getting Epperson a lengthy sentence.” Senior United States District Judge William J. Martinez presided over the sentencing. The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Denver Police Department handled the investigation. Assistant United States Attorney Miles Robinson handled the prosecution. Case Number: 25-cr-245-WJM Contact USACO.PublicAffairs@usdoj.gov Updated November 9, 2026 Component USAO - Colorado

title: St. Mark Arson Suspects Arraigned On Firearm and Ammunition Charges
body: Press Release St. Mark Arson Suspects Arraigned On Firearm and Ammunition Charges Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Michigan FLINT – Sonja L. Settles, 50 of Flint, and Billy J. Chambers, 63 of Flint, were arraigned last week on a second superseding indictment, which added new firearm and ammunition charges against the pair, to their previous charges related to the arson of St. Mark Missionary Baptist Church, announced United States Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon Jr. Joining in the announcement was James Deir, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives (ATF) – Detroit Field Division. The second superseding indictment charged Settles with being a felon in possession of a firearm and Chambers with being a felon in possession of ammunition. Court records allege that in the early morning hours of August 30, 2025, Settles and Chambers spoke by phone. A short time later, around 2:03 a.m., Chambers walked to St. Mark Missionary Baptist Church from a nearby field east of the building. He looked around the area where the fire would later be started. Chambers went back into the field and returned around 2:11 a.m. carrying an object in his right hand. He used it to break a church window and then walked back to the field. About a minute later, Chambers returned carrying a piece of cloth and a red gasoline can hidden inside a black garbage bag. He poured gasoline through the broken window, placed the cloth in the window opening, and poured more gasoline inside. At about 2:13 a.m., Chambers went back to the nearby field and threw away the gas can, which was still inside the garbage bag. Three minutes later, around 2:16 a.m., he returned to the church carrying a device used to start a fire. He lit the device and used it to ignite the gasoline, setting the church on fire. About four minutes after the fire started, around 2:20 a.m., Chambers called Settles. Phone records show that Chambers' cellphone connected to a tower located less than half a mile from the church. At the same time, Settles' cellphone connected to another nearby cell tower in the area of the church. The Flint Fire Department responded and put out the fire. The blaze caused about $350,000 in damage, and the church was unable to hold regular worship services for about two months while repairs were made. The new charges are alleged to have occurred on March 10, 2026 (Settles), and June 5, 2026 (Chambers). This case was investigated by special agents of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, with assistance from the Flint Police Department. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Anthony Vance. An indictment is only a charge and is not evidence of guilt.  The defendant is entitled to a fair trial in which it will be the government’s burden to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. Ohio Woman Sentenced for Not Paying Employment Taxes
body: Press Release Ohio Woman Sentenced for Not Paying Employment Taxes Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio AKRON, Ohio – A 51-year-old woman was sentenced for issuing payments to herself, using funds withheld from paychecks, instead of making required quarterly employment tax payments. Brenna Butdorf, 51, of Wooster, has been sentenced to 18 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, after pleading guilty to Failing to Truthfully Account for and Pay Over Trust Fund Taxes. She was also ordered to pay a $55,000 fine, $198,448.75 in restitution to the IRS, and an additional $147,992.50 to another victim as a condition of her supervised release. According to court documents, Butdorf managed the finances of an electrical contracting company that her husband owned and that was based out of their home. Federal law requires such companies to withhold social security, Medicare, and federal income taxes from employees’ paychecks and then remit them  to the United States. In her role as accountant and office manager for her husband’s business, Butdorf withheld these taxes from the company’s employees. Instead of remitting the funds to the IRS, however, Butdorf issued payments to herself and her husband, which were funded by the unremitted employment tax withholdings. Butdorf then spent these proceeds on herself and her family, including purchasing  a condominium in Florida, and paying dues for a private camp, shooting club, and vacations. In total, investigators discovered that from 2015 to 2021, Butdorf failed to pay more than $494,000 in employment taxes to the government. The investigation was conducted by the IRS-Criminal Investigation Division’s Cleveland office. Assistant United States Attorney Megan R. Miller led the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. Contact Jessica Salas Novak Jessica.Salas.Novak@usdoj.gov Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Tax Components National Fraud Enforcement Division USAO - Ohio, Northern

title: Rutland Man Sentenced to 89 Months for Distribution and Possession of Child Sexual Abuse Material
body: Press Release Rutland Man Sentenced to 89 Months for Distribution and Possession of Child Sexual Abuse Material Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Vermont USAVT.Press@usdoj.gov BURLINGTON – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Vermont stated that on November 6, 2026, Matthew Kielecki, 45, of Rutland, Vermont, was sentenced by Chief United States District Judge Christina Reiss to a term of 89 months’ imprisonment to be followed by a 10-year term of supervised release. Kielecki previously pleaded guilty to distribution and possession of child sexual abuse material (“CSAM”) on July 7, 2026. According to court records, in March of 2025, Kielecki uploaded to a social media messaging platform 23 files containing CSAM. The CSAM depicted the sexual assaults of children ranging in age from younger than 8 years old to younger than 12 years old. Kielecki also communicated with other social media users interested in CSAM, in one case, suggesting that he had produced CSAM over the internet with a 12-year-old girl, and in other, encouraging another person to view CSAM over that person’s stated reluctance. When law enforcement executed a search warrant at Kielecki’s home in September 2025, they recovered psilocybin mushrooms, 30 marijuana plants in various stages of growth, and 20 firearms, two of which were loaded. Evidence from Kielecki’s phone suggested that he was engaged in distributing marijuana in violation of both federal and state law. Law enforcement also discovered on Kielecki’s cellphone additional CSAM depicting a prepubescent female child. First Assistant United States Attorney Jonathan A. Ophardt commended the collaborative investigatory efforts of Homeland Security Investigations, the Vermont Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, the Rutland City Police Department, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, and the Drug Enforcement Administration. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Corinne Smith. Kielecki was represented by Assistant Federal Public Defender Sam Ansell. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . title: Panga Boat Pilots Sentenced in Maritime Smuggling Event that Killed Four in Homeland Security Task Force Case
body: Press Release Panga Boat Pilots Sentenced in Maritime Smuggling Event that Killed Four in Homeland Security Task Force Case Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California Kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO – Jesus Ivan Rodriguez Leyva and Julio Cesar Zuniga Luna, both Mexican nationals, were sentenced in federal court today to 70 months in prison for piloting a panga which overturned near Del Mar, California in May 2025, resulting in the deaths of two Mexican national adults and two minors, ages 14 and 10, from India. “Today’s sentences reflect the serious consequences of placing greed above human life,” said U.S, Attorney Adam Gordon. Panga with cracked engine held together by duct tape was recovered at the beach “This sentencing follows an extensive investigation and the coordinated efforts of the Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) San Diego Marine Task Force and our law enforcement partners to hold human smugglers accountable for the devastating consequences of their actions,” said Kevin Murphy, Special Agent in Charge of HSI San Diego. “This case underscores the critical role of our partnerships in responding to maritime smuggling events, conducting complex investigations, and pursuing those who endanger lives for financial gain.” “Human smuggling organizations continue to show a reckless disregard for human life,” said U.S. Border Patrol San Diego Sector Chief Patrol Agent Justin De La Torre. “This tragedy underscores the deadly consequences of maritime smuggling and our continued commitment, alongside our law enforcement partners, to hold those responsible accountable.” Rodriguez and Zuniga pleaded guilty on April 14, 2026, to two counts of attempted bringing in illegal aliens resulting in death as well as two counts of attempted bringing in illegal aliens for financial gain. In a related case, three load drivers pleaded guilty to conspiring with others to transport and move aliens within the United States. Plea documents outlined an overarching conspiracy in which individuals in Mexico recruited drivers to assist in smuggling aliens into the United States by meeting maritime vessels transporting illegal aliens upon their arrival into the United States, concealing them in vehicles, taking them to load houses, and then further transporting them to their intended destinations within the United States.  The load drivers coordinated with these Mexico-based co-conspirators as well as with co-conspirators in the United States. The load drivers have already been sentenced. Please see 25-cr-02056-BJC. According to Rodriguez’s and Zuniga’s plea agreements, each admitted that they “piloted” the vessel from Mexico into the United States on May 5, 2025, with 19 aliens aboard, including three minors; that the vessel had no running lights or radio; was overloaded with more passengers than the panga could safely hold; and that the aliens aboard were only given trash bags to cover their clothes and were not properly outfitted for the voyage. They further admitted that after the panga left Popotla, Mexico, the motor experienced issues and they were forced to return to their launch site where the motor was quickly repaired, and they set sail once again for the United States. According to the plea agreement, as the panga approached the beach in Del Mar, Rodriguez and Zuniga told the aliens to remove their life jackets to make it easier to exit the panga and run to waiting vehicles. Unfortunately, when the panga was approximately 200 yards from United States shores, the motor yet again failed and the vessel capsized in the surf. Onlookers watched and filmed the event as law enforcement was notified. Homeland Security Investigations San Diego Marine Task Force, the U.S. Coast Guard, local lifeguards, and U.S. Border Patrol initiated a joint search and rescue operation. Ultimately, four undocumented aliens were located on the beach and were transported for medical care and three more were found deceased on the scene, including one minor. On May 21, 2025, a human foot was found on the shoreline near Torrey Pines State Beach. A DNA test was conducted and it was determined to belong to a 10-year-old who had been on the panga, bringing the death toll to four. During today’s hearing, U.S. District Judge Benjamin J. Cheeks told one of the defendants: “This case is a tragedy all around …As a result of your actions, there are four people who are no longer here on this planet. Four people who are no longer here to hold their family members, who are no longer here to enjoy life, to breathe the air.” This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jill Streja, Sean Van Demark, Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Danielle Hickman and former Assistant U.S. Attorney Edward Chang. DEFENDANTS Case Number 25cr2057-BJC Julio Cesar Zuniga Luna                                 Age: 32                                  Mexico Jesus Ivan Rodriguez Leyva                           Age: 28                                   Mexico SUMMARY OF CHARGES Attempted Bringing in Aliens Resulting in Death – Title 8, U.S.C., Sections 1324(a)(1)(A)(i), (v)(II), and (a)(1)(B)(iv) Maximum penalty: Death or Life in Prison and $250,000 fine Bringing in Aliens for Financial Gain – Title 8, U.S.C., Section 1324(a)(2)(B)(ii) Maximum penalty: Ten years in prison with a three-year mandatory minimum and $250,000 fine INVESTIGATING AGENCIES Homeland Security Investigations – Marine Task Force U.S. Border Patrol U.S. Customs and Border Protection – Air and Marine Operations United States Coast Guard San Diego Lifeguard Service San Diego County Medical Examiner’s Office Contact Kelly Thornton, Director of Media Relations Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Human Smuggling Component USAO - California, Southern Press Release Number: CAS26-1109-Rodriguez

title: LEAD Awards Again Honor Outstanding Performance of Numerous District Law Enforcement Officers and Agencies, Federal Prosecutors
body: Press Release LEAD Awards Again Honor Outstanding Performance of Numerous District Law Enforcement Officers and Agencies, Federal Prosecutors Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Pennsylvania PITTSBURGH, Pa. - The Law Enforcement Agency Directors (LEAD) of Western Pennsylvania recognized law enforcement officers and prosecutors from across nearly a dozen agencies during the 28th Annual LEAD Awards ceremony, announced United States Attorney Troy Rivetti. Comprising the Western Pennsylvania heads of federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies, LEAD bestows awards annually as a way of recognizing outstanding performance from law enforcement agents and officers, as well as prosecutors. This year’s awards included: The Lifetime Service Award was presented to Michael C. Warfield (retired) for his outstanding service to law enforcement across three decades, including 25 years as a Trooper with the Pennsylvania State Police (PSP) and several years as the Law Enforcement Coordinator with the United States Attorney’s Office (USAO) for the Western District of Pennsylvania. For 18 of his years with the PSP, Warfield served as a Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) federally deputized Task Force Officer, in which role he led numerous successful wiretap investigations of large-scale drug traffickers, including overseeing the district’s first roving wiretap investigation (allowing agents to immediately intercept a target’s next phone upon the target’s discarding of his previous one). In 2019, the USAO hired Warfield as the office’s Law Enforcement Coordinator, where he advised office leadership on law enforcement issues throughout the district’s 25 counties and facilitated improved working relationships, crime prevention efforts, and trainings among federal, state and local law enforcement until his 2022 retirement and move to the private sector. The Federal Bureau of Investigation’s (FBI) Greater Pittsburgh Safe Streets Task Force, DEA, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), U.S. Marshals Service, Pittsburgh Bureau of Police, Allegheny County Sheriff’s Office, Allegheny County Police Department (ACPD), and USAO received a team award for their investigation and prosecution of an individual who attempted to murder a DEA Special Agent. The evidence revealed that the defendant fired 18 rounds from a semiautomatic firearm at the DEA Special Agent while the agent was conducting surveillance in a drug trafficking investigation. While many of those shots struck the DEA Special Agent’s vehicle, the agent himself fortunately was not injured. The multi-agency response, and FBI investigation that followed, brought about the prompt identification, arrest, and federal indictment of the individual for the attempted murder of the DEA Special Agent, along with federal narcotics and firearms offenses. A federal search warrant for the actor’s residence and the vehicle used in the shooting resulted in the seizure of more than 100 bricks of fentanyl, a 9mm Glock pistol equipped with a 50 round drum magazine, and other evidence. The defendant has pleaded guilty and will be sentenced later this year. Special Agent John Orlando, Task Force Officer Scott Patterson, and Operational Support Technician Rochelle Nestel from the FBI, Task Force Officers Thomas Costa and Jeffrey Morrell from the DEA, Inspector Jason Parillo of the United States Postal Inspection Service, and Assistant U.S. Attorney (AUSA) Craig Haller of the USAO received a team award for outstanding performance for their investigation and prosecution of a large-scale drug trafficking organization following a series of overdoses, including one fatal overdose, in Mercer County, Pennsylvania. The investigation resulted in eight federal indictments and arrests, the seizure of more than three kilograms of cocaine/crack cocaine, over 500 grams of heroin/fentanyl, approximately $180,000 in forfeitures, and 19 firearms. The defendants collectively received 921 months of federal imprisonment, including a 480-month (40-year) sentence for the lead defendant in the case. FBI Task Force Officer (TFO) Patterson additionally was recognized with an individual LEAD award for his invaluable contributions to the FBI North Country Task Force over the past six years. This included TFO Patterson playing a significant role in the successful investigation and prosecution of numerous complex federal narcotics trafficking organizations, serving as both a primary case agent and co-case agent on a wide range of important investigations targeting the community’s most serious offenders. An individual LEAD award was presented to AUSA Maureen Sheehan-Balchon of the USAO for her lead role in the prosecution of two men—both of whom this year were sentenced to life in federal prison—for the premeditated brutal murder of a woman by explosive device. The evidence in the case showed that a bomb exploded inside the victim’s Clearfield, Pennsylvania, apartment, fatally injuring the woman and destroying the apartment building by the resulting fire. AUSA Sheehan-Balchon and her team of colleagues and ATF investigators oversaw a meticulous, multi-year investigation to determine the origin, cause, and motive behind the explosion and to prosecute those responsible for the horrific crime. During separate lengthy jury trials, AUSA Sheehan-Balchon and her team offered extensive evidence tying the defendants to the bombing, including presenting several witnesses that testified about the lead defendant’s threats and intimidation against the victim and others. ATF Special Agent Marc Wilner received an award for his leadership in investigating an individual who committed numerous violent crimes within the Western District of Pennsylvania, including the armed robbery of a hemp dispensary and a street shooting several weeks later, using the same vehicle. As a result of the work of Special Agent Wilner and his ATF team and community partners, the suspect was federally indicted on charges of Hobbs Act robbery, possession of a firearm in furtherance of a crime of violence, and being a felon in possession of a firearm, in addition to also being charged in county courts with attempted homicide, receiving stolen property, and aggravated assault. Detectives David Ernst and Quoc Vo of the ACPD were recognized for leading an investigation into a series of coordinated burglaries targeting federally licensed firearms dealers, during which the detectives identified connections between the burglaries and several additional offenses, including vehicle thefts and attempted break-ins throughout the area, and recovered 55 of the stolen firearms. The year-long investigation resulted in charges against eight individuals, totaling 1,433 criminal offenses. Special Agent Derek Bassler from Homeland Security Investigations was the recipient of an individual LEAD award for heading an investigation into the narcotics distribution and money laundering activities of a Western Pennsylvania resident. After determining that the suspect had been taking a bus to New York City to purchase narcotics, Special Agent Bassler organized a multi-agency and multi-state surveillance detail to observe the individual on such a trip and ultimately effect a traffic stop upon the defendant’s return to Western Pennsylvania, which resulted in the seizure of more than five kilograms of cocaine and 31 grams of methamphetamine. The defendant subsequently pleaded guilty in federal court to charges of drug trafficking and money laundering, with forfeiture of cryptocurrency and a residential property. LEAD is composed of the following law enforcement agencies: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives; Drug Enforcement Administration; Federal Bureau of Investigation; U.S. Attorney’s Office, Western District of Pennsylvania; Homeland Security Investigations; Internal Revenue Service - Criminal Investigation; U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Transportation Security Administration; U.S. Department of Defense - Defense Criminal Investigative Service; U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development; U.S. Marshals Service; U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General; U.S. Postal Inspection Service; U.S. Probation & Pretrial Services; United States Secret Service; U.S. Social Security Administration – Office of Inspector General; U.S. Department of State – Diplomatic Security Service; U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Air Marshal Service; U.S. Department of Transportation - Office of Inspector General; U.S. Department of Veterans Administration - Office of Inspector General; U.S. Department of Labor - Office of Inspector General; U.S. Department of Agriculture - Office of Inspector General; U.S. Department of Homeland Security – Federal Protective Service; U.S. Food and Drug Administration – Office of Criminal Investigations; Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General; Pennsylvania State Police; Pennsylvania Board of Probation and Parole; Western Pennsylvania Chiefs of Police Association; Allegheny County Police Department; Allegheny County Sheriff’s Office; Allegheny County District Attorney’s Office; Allegheny County Chiefs of Police Association; Allegheny County Housing Authority Police Department; Port Authority of Allegheny County Police Department; Washington County District Attorney’s Office; Westmoreland County District Attorney’s Office; Pittsburgh Bureau of Police; Mt. title: North Carolina Man Indicted for Mailing Antisemitic Threats to Jewish Organizations and Secret Service Protectees in South Florida
body: Press Release North Carolina Man Indicted for Mailing Antisemitic Threats to Jewish Organizations and Secret Service Protectees in South Florida Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Florida MIAMI – A federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida has returned an indictment against Brian Charles, 58, for allegedly mailing antisemitic letters threatening violence against Jewish organizations and individuals protected by the U.S. Secret Service. According to court records, Charles, who was staying in the Charlotte, North Carolina, area at the time of the alleged offense, was arrested and made his initial appearance before a U.S. Magistrate Judge in the Western District of North Carolina. Upon arrival in the Southern District of Florida, Charles was ordered detained by the court. In July 2026, Charles, allegedly mailed threatening letters to officers and executives of the Holocaust Memorial Miami Beach, the American Jewish Committee’s Palm Beach office, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, as well as two Secret Service protectees. All of the letters were mailed to recipients in the Southern District of Florida. The letters contained identical antisemitic messages, including a graphic image and threats of violence against Jewish people. Charles is charged with mailing threatening communications. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in federal prison. Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas for the Southern District of Florida and Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement. FBI Miami is investigating the case, with assistance from the U.S. Secret Service.  Acting U.S. Attorney Lorenzo Klukas also thanked the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of North Carolina for their assistance on this matter. Assistant U.S. Attorney Edward N. Stamm is prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.sdfl.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.sdfl.uscourts.gov , under case number 26-cr-20411. ### Contact Public Affairs Unit U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of Florida USAFLS.News@usdoj.gov Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component USAO - Florida, Southern

title: Convicted Double-Murderer Sentenced to Prison for Federal Gun Crime
body: Press Release Convicted Double-Murderer Sentenced to Prison for Federal Gun Crime Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of West Virginia BLUEFIELD, W.Va. – Casey Rygh, 48, of Rochester, Minnesota, was sentenced today to three years and 10 months in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release, for being a felon in possession of a firearm. According to court documents and statements made in court, on August 25, 2025, law enforcement officers captured Rygh as part of Operation Rolling Waters, a warrant and fugitive sweep, in the Matoaka area of Mercer County, West Virginia. Officers found Rygh possessed a loaded SCCY Model CPX-2 9mm pistol in his waistband. Federal law prohibits a person with a prior felony conviction from possessing a firearm or ammunition. Rygh knew he was prohibited from possessing a firearm because of his prior felony convictions for two counts of felony murder and conspiracy to commit aggravated robbery in Logan County, West Virginia, Circuit Court on December 15, 1997. United States Attorney Moore Capito made the announcement and commended the investigative work of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the United States Marshals Service (USMS), and its Cops United Felony Fugitive Enforcement Division (CUFFED) Task Force of Southern West Virginia. Senior United States District Judge David A. Faber imposed the sentence. Assistant United States Attorney Brian D. Parsons prosecuted the case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. title: Lucas County Man Sentenced to 14 Years in Prison for Coercion, Enticement, and Child Pornography Charges
body: Press Release Lucas County Man Sentenced to 14 Years in Prison for Coercion, Enticement, and Child Pornography Charges Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio TOLEDO, Ohio – A 40-year-old man has been sentenced to federal prison for arranging to engage in illicit sexual conduct with a purported 12-year-old boy and for Child Sexual Abuse Materials (CSAM) charges. Eben Vondruska, of Toledo, was sentenced to 168 months (14 years) in prison by U.S. District Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick, after pleading guilty in July to: •    Coercion or Enticement of a Minor •    Receipt and Distribution of Child Pornography, or CSAM Vondruska was also ordered to serve 15 years of supervised release after imprisonment and pay $10,000 toward the Justice for Victims of Trafficking Act, which was established in 2015 to provide justice for victims of trafficking. According to court documents, Toledo law enforcement was investigating suspected Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) activity on an online platform—that was also distributed to an undercover agent—and Vondruska was subsequently identified. He was communicating online with an undercover agent who purported to have a 12-year-old son and indicated his desire to meet the fictitious boy at a prearranged location for the purpose of engaging in illegal sexual conduct with him. When Vondruska arrived at the agreed-upon location, he was apprehended by law enforcement and taken into custody. During a search warrant executed at his residence, Vondruska’s electronic devices were seized and forensically examined. Investigators found that from about September 2025 to February 2026, he knowingly distributed visual depictions of minors engaged in sexually explicit conduct. Additionally, investigators learned that Vondruska had  prior criminal convictions for sexual offenses in 2011 and 2013 in Xenia, Ohio, and that he had failed to register as a sex offender there. The investigation was led by the FBI Toledo Resident Agency’s Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force and the Toledo Police Department. Assistant United States Attorneys Sara Al-Sorghali and Frank Spryszak led the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. The initiative is led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices throughout the country and marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, visit justice.gov/PSC. To report child exploitation, please visit cybertipline.org , or call 1-800-843-5678, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Contact Jessica Salas Novak Jessica.Salas.Novak@usdoj.gov Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Ohio, Northern

title: Department of Justice Recognizes Three U.S. Attorney's Office Employees With Director's Award
body: Press Release Department of Justice Recognizes Three U.S. Attorney's Office Employees With Director's Award Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – United States Attorney Leah B. Foley announced that three employees of the U.S. Attorney’s Office were selected as recipients of the 2026 Executive Office for United States Attorneys (EOUSA) Director’s Award. The Director’s Award recognizes excellence across the U.S. Attorney community and honors the exceptional contributions to the Justice Department’s mission by attorneys and support personnel, serving in the nation’s 94 federal districts. The following individuals were recognized at the award ceremony in Washington, D.C. on Oct. 28, 2026: Special Assistant United States Attorney James Nagelberg Excellence as a Special Assistant United States Attorney James Nagelberg served as a Special Assistant United States Attorney (SAUSA) from January 2023 to June 2026, becoming a leading authority on Social Security fraud investigations and prosecutions. He vetted criminal referrals to maximize the Office’s effectiveness in combatting benefit fraud, contributing to the recovery of over $1.4 million in restitution and pretrial diversion payments and securing more than $925,000 in forfeiture money judgments. Mr. Nagelberg obtained the district’s first voter fraud conviction in a $400,000 identity theft case. He also helped expand the Social Security Administration’s SAUSA program nationwide and mentored SAUSAs across the country, strengthening national and district efforts to combat benefit fraud. Assistant United States Attorney Donald Lockhart Excellence as an Appellate Assistant United States Attorney Donald Lockhart serves as Chief of the Appellate Unit and leads a highly respected appellate team, reviewing numerous filings and offering insight drawn from a decades-long career in public service. Mr. Lockhart has argued complicated government appeals delivering top-tier advocacy. His experience and expertise have made him a nationally recognized appellate attorney, teaching and collaborating with the Appellate Chiefs’ Working Group and engaging with the Solicitor General’s Office. Under Mr. Lockhart’s guidance, the Appellate Unit has secured favorable opinions from the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit in several notable cases, including: United States v. Salemme ; United States v. Vavic ; United States v. Coleman ; United States v. Correa ; United States v. Pullman & Lynch ; and United States v. Cromwell . Lizzette Ospina-Yemo Superior Performance in Administration Lizzette Ospina-Yemo has been an essential leader in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Massachusetts since joining as Human Resources Officer in 2014 and becoming Deputy Administrative Officer in 2023. She expertly manages wide-ranging responsibilities across HR, finance, IT, security, facilities and procurement. Her leadership has strengthened accountability and improved processes across all administrative areas. Ms. Ospina-Yemo has navigated complex employee relations and challenges such as federal shutdowns, deferred resignation programs, credible threats to U.S. Attorney’s Office employees and the loss of a colleague with professionalism and compassion. Her dedication, steady judgment and commitment to the mission make her an invaluable asset to the district and the broader U.S. Attorney’s Office community. “The success of our office is made possible by the extraordinary dedication and professionalism of the people who serve the District of Massachusetts every day,” said U.S. Attorney Leah B. Foley. “Mr. Nagelberg, Mr. Lockhart and Ms. Ospina-Yemo have each distinguished themselves through exceptional service, leadership and commitment to the Department of Justice’s mission. Their contributions have strengthened our office, advanced justice and benefited the people we serve. Their dedication to excellence, integrity and public service exemplifies the very best of our office, and I am proud to see their achievements recognized with this well-deserved honor.” Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Office and Personnel Updates Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: United States Attorney's Office Files Civil Forfeiture Action to Recover Cryptocurrency Involved in Romance Fraud Schemes
body: Press Release United States Attorney's Office Files Civil Forfeiture Action to Recover Cryptocurrency Involved in Romance Fraud Schemes Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Scammers targeted individuals on online dating sites and Facebook BOSTON – The United States Attorney’s Office has filed a civil forfeiture action to recover 456,602 USDT (Tether), alleged to be proceeds of romance fraud schemes targeting individuals in Massachusetts and elsewhere on online dating sites and Facebook. The cryptocurrency currently has an estimated value of approximately $456,602. As alleged in the complaint, after cultivating a relationship of trust online, victims were introduced to cryptocurrency and encouraged to make investments on fake cryptocurrency platforms. Although victims believed they were sending funds to a legitimate cryptocurrency investment platform and earning profits, in reality those funds were sent to unhosted cryptocurrency wallets (wallets not hosted on a cryptocurrency exchange). When the victim attempted to withdraw funds but could not, even after paying additional funds for so-called fees and taxes, they realized it was a scam. The scam proceeds were traced to two cryptocurrency wallets and the funds were seized by authorities. It is a violation of federal law to use wire communications as part of a scheme to defraud or to obtain money or property by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, and property traceable to such fraud is subject to forfeiture. It is also a violation of federal law to conduct a financial transaction knowing that the transaction is designed to conceal the nature, location, source, ownership, or control of criminal proceeds, and property involved in such transactions is subject to forfeiture. A civil forfeiture action allows third parties to assert claims to property, which must be resolved before the property can be forfeited to the United States and returned to victims. This is one of several civil forfeiture actions the U.S. Attorney’s Office has filed seeking to forfeit cryptocurrency traced to fraud schemes targeting Massachusetts victims. Members of the public who believe they are victims of a cybercrime. including cryptocurrency scams, tech support scams, investment scams and business email compromise fraud scams, should contact USAMA.CyberTip@usdoj.gov . United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation Boston Field Office made the announcement today. Assistant U.S. Attorney Carole E. Head, Chief of the Asset Recovery Unit is prosecuting the civil forfeiture action. The details contained in the civil forfeiture complaint are allegations. body: Press Release Columbia County Man Pleads Guilty to Unlawful Firearm Dealing to Mexico Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Gainesville, Florida – Jose Manuel Barron, 32, of Columbia County, Florida, has pleaded guilty in federal court on a charge of conspiracy to transfer firearms to a nonresident and making false statements to a firearms dealer. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida announced the guilty plea. According to court records, between June 2019 and February 2022, the defendant agreed to transfer, sell, and deliver multiple firearms to an intended recipient in Mexico. Barron acquired one of the firearms under false pretenses from a federal firearms dealer. Three of the firearms were later recovered in Culiacan, Sinaloa, Mexico. Sentencing is scheduled for January 26, 2027, at 3:00pm before Chief United States District Court Judge Allen C. Winsor in Gainesville, Florida. The defendant faces up to five years of imprisonment. The case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Adam Hapner. title: Las Vegas Man Sentenced to Seven Years in Prison for Trafficking Methamphetamine and Fentanyl, and Money Laundering
body: Press Release Las Vegas Man Sentenced to Seven Years in Prison for Trafficking Methamphetamine and Fentanyl, and Money Laundering Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – A Las Vegas man was sentenced today by United States District Judge Cristina D. Silva to 84 months in prison to be followed by three years of supervised release for his role in a conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and fentanyl, and to launder thousands of dollars of drug proceeds to Mexico. The government recommended a sentence of 84 months in prison. “Fentanyl is a weapon of mass destruction in our communities, and those who traffic it are dealing in pure death,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “The defendant poured thousands of these lethal pills onto our streets with a callous disregard for human life, caring only about his bottom line. Every single ounce he distributed was a potential overdose and a shattered family. We will remain relentless and aggressive in hunting down anyone who pushes this poison into our neighborhoods, and we will ensure they spend a very long time behind federal bars.” “Methamphetamine and fentanyl continue to devastate American communities,” David Olesky, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration Los Angeles Field Division, which covers Nevada. “Traffickers exploit our neighborhoods for profit, but today’s sentencing serves as a reminder that drug crimes will be met with strict accountability and zero tolerance. The DEA remains committed to working with our HSTF partners to cut off drug flows and block the money laundering networks funding Mexican drug operations.” According to court documents, between June 2025 and January 14, 2026, Efrain Cabada-Martinez conspired with co-defendants Juan Carlos Cabada-Mendoza, Isaac Theojaris Tapia-Cabada, and others to distribute methamphetamine and fentanyl in Las Vegas. Additionally, Cabada-Martinez conspired with employees at a money services business in Las Vegas to send drug proceeds from Las Vegas to drug suppliers in Mexico. Cabada-Martinez pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering. The DEA investigated this case. Assistant United States Attorney Joshua Brister prosecuted the case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. title: New York woman sentenced to 3 years in prison for selling diet pills laced with meth
body: Press Release New York woman sentenced to 3 years in prison for selling diet pills laced with meth Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Montana BILLINGS – A New York woman who sold counterfeit diet pills that she laced with meth was sentenced Friday to three years in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, U.S. Attorney Scott Twito said. U.S. District Judge William W. Mercer presided. Carrie Ann Taylor, 50, pleaded guilty in March 2026 to mail fraud. The government alleged in court documents that Taylor was selling diet pills laced with methamphetamine through eBay. A Billings man submitted an online tip on Sept. 5, 2023, saying he had ordered “Skald” brand diet pills on eBay in February 2023 and started taking them in May. The man was drug tested by his employer in June and failed the test, leaving him suspicious of the diet pills he’d ordered. Law enforcement collected what was left of the “Skald” diet pills and found they tested positive for meth. Taylor also mailed six bottles of diet pills labelled “Skald Oxydynamic Fat Scorcher” to a woman in Montana in March 2023. The woman told law enforcement that she used the pills for several months but did not experience weight loss, so she stopped. She handed over what she had to investigators, who found all the pills contained meth. On April 3, 2024, an undercover agent ordered two kinds of diet pills from Taylor’s eBay account, “PhenQ Ultra” and “PhenGold.” Both orders were sent to Billings, and both tested positive for meth. At the same time, investigators ordered bottles of “PhenQ Ultra” and “PhenGold” directly from the manufacturers; both tested negative for meth. Investigators then learned Taylor sent another woman in Randolph, Wisconsin, illicit diet pills, which also tested positive for meth. In total, law enforcement collected pills from five separate shipments between 2023 and 2024. Every pill tested positive for meth. Taylor fraudulently sold the pills by falsely claiming they were legitimate diet supplements manufactured by real supplement companies. The pills were shipped and delivered in bottles falsely labelled as these products. Several customers told Taylor her pills were counterfeit and one manufacturer sent her a cease-and-desist notice for using counterfeit versions of its products. Tayor’s scheme resulted in serious harm. A member of the U.S. Army used the pills and tested positive for meth during a random urinalysis. He had to spend significant amounts of money hiring a lawyer to defend himself against drug abuse allegations. Another victim was fired from his job after testing positive for meth following a workplace drug test. During the entire scheme, Taylor sold approximately 1,517 bottles of counterfeit diet pills and made about $56,454 in profits. Assistant U.S. Attorney Colin Rubich prosecuted the case. The FBI conducted the investigation. title: D.C. Man Sentenced for Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release D.C. Man Sentenced for Possession of Child Pornography Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON –Angel Anthony Rios, 29, of the District of Columbia, was sentenced Friday, November 6, in U.S. District Court to 46 months in federal prison in connection with distributing videos of child sexual abuse materials over the internet, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Rios pleaded guilty on August 14, 2026, before Judge Beryl A. Howell to one count of possession of child pornography. In addition to the 46-month prison sentence, Judge Howell ordered Rios to serve six years of supervised release. According to court documents, beginning on Dec. 18, 2025, Rios exchanged messages with another user on social media regarding a variety of topics including politics. Rios ultimately revealed that he had a sexual interest in children. Subsequently, Rios distributed videos depicting the abuse of a three-year-old boy. During the course of his communications, Rios stated, “Kids are here to be used, and I don’t mean that ironically.” Law enforcement arrested Rios on Jan. 23, 2026. Joining U.S. Attorney Pirro in the announcement was FBI Assistant Director in Charge Darren B. Cox of the Washington Field Office. This case is being investigated by FBI’s Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Janani Iyengar. This case was brought as part of the Department of Justice's Project Safe Childhood initiative. In February 2006, the Attorney General created Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative designed to protect children from online exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorney's Offices, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as identify and rescue victims. title: New Orleans Man Indicted for Violating Federal Controlled Substances Act
body: Press Release New Orleans Man Indicted for Violating Federal Controlled Substances Act Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS, LA – On October 16, 2026, DOMINICK CURRY ("CURRY") , age 41, of New Orleans, was charged in a recently unsealed indictment with possession with intent to distribute controlled substances, in violation of Title 21, United States Code, Sections 841(a)(1), 841(b)(1)(A), and 841(b)(1)(B), announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. According to court records, on September 3, 2026, CURRY possessed, with intent to distribute, 400 grams or more of a mixture and substance containing fentanyl; and more than 50 grams of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine. If convicted of Count 1 of the indictment, possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl, CURRY faces a minimum term of ten (10) years up to a maximum term of life imprisonment, a fine of up to $10,000,000, and at least five (5) years of supervised release. If convicted of Count 2 of the indictment, possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine, CURRY faces a minimum term of five (5) years up to a maximum term of forty (40) years imprisonment, a fine of up to $5,000,000, and at least four (4) years of supervised release.  He also faces payment of a $100 mandatory special assessment fee for each charged offense. U.S. Attorney Courcelle reiterated that the indictment is merely a charge and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. The case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms; New Orleans Police Department; and the Slidell Police Department.  It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul J. Hubbell, I.V. of the Narcotics Unit. This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), a program bringing together all levels of law enforcement and the communities they serve to reduce violent crime and gun violence, and to make our neighborhoods safer for everyone. On May 26, 2021, the Department launched a violent crime reduction strategy strengthening PSN based on these core principles: fostering trust and legitimacy in our communities, supporting community-based organizations that help prevent violence from occurring in the first place, setting focused and strategic enforcement priorities, and measuring the results. title: Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Leads to Indictment of Multiple Defendants in Fentanyl-Related Death Case
body: Press Release Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Leads to Indictment of Multiple Defendants in Fentanyl-Related Death Case Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Utah SALT LAKE CITY, Utah – A 15-count indictment has been unsealed charging multiple individuals for their alleged roles in an organized criminal enterprise involving several drug-trafficking offenses, including the distribution of fentanyl that resulted in the death of another person. Christopher Lee Washington, 53, of Millcreek, Utah; Natasha Annette Ashworth, 39, of Salt Lake City; Keisha Brewer-Case, 23, of West Valley City, Utah; Brittany Cuevas Caldwell, 38, of Salt Lake City; and Keith Jerome Lewis, 59, of Salt Lake City, were indicted by a federal grand jury on October 21, 2026, in the District of Utah. According to court documents, beginning on a date unknown, but not later than April 29, 2026, and continuing through at least August 27, 2026, in the District of Utah and elsewhere, all five defendants conspired to distribute four hundred grams or more of a substance containing fentanyl; five hundred grams or more of a mixture of a substance containing methamphetamine; and cocaine. As alleged in court documents, on June 23, 2026, Washington intentionally distributed fentanyl, which resulted in the death of another person. Additionally, according to court documents, as part of the investigation, on August 27, 2026, while executing a search warrant on Ashworth’s residence, agents recovered approximately 19 pounds of methamphetamine, a brick of cocaine weighing approximately one kilogram, and approximately 21 grams of fentanyl powder. Drugs seized during the execution of a search warrant on August 27, 2026. Washington, Ashworth, Brewer-Case, Caldwell, and Lewis are charged with conspiracy to distribute fentanyl, conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine, and conspiracy to distribute cocaine. Washington is also charged with distribution of fentanyl resulting in death. Additional charges pertaining to the individual defendants are detailed in the indictment. Initial appearances have occurred or are scheduled throughout November 2026 before U.S. Magistrate Judge Daphne A. Oberg at the Orrin G. Hatch United States Courthouse in downtown Salt Lake City. United States Attorney Melissa Holyoak of the District of Utah made the announcement. The case is being investigated jointly by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Salt Lake City Police Department, and Unified Police Department of Greater Salt Lake. Assistant United States Attorney Vernon G. Stejskal of the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Utah is prosecuting the case. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Salt Lake comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Utah.
