body: Press Release Medina County Man Sentenced to 13 Years in Prison for Child Pornography Charges Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio Anree-Julian McKhoni, of Brunswick, was sentenced to 160 months (13.3 years) in prison by U.S. District Judge Solomon Oliver, after pleading guilty in June to: •    Receipt and Distribution of Visual Depictions of Real Minors Engaged in Sexually Explicit Conduct, and •    Child Pornography McKhoni was also ordered to serve eight years of supervised release after imprisonment and pay $10,000 toward the Justice for Victims of Trafficking Act, which was established in 2015 to provide justice for victims of trafficking. According to court documents and evidence, law enforcement was investigating suspected Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) activity on an online platform and McKhoni was identified. During a search warrant executed at his Medina County residence in July 2023, investigators discovered a sophisticated computer setup and seized electronic devices for forensic examination. Investigators found McKhoni was in possession of more than 20,000 visual depictions of minors engaged in sexually explicit conduct, including over 3,000 files of sadistic or masochistic conduct. Additionally, investigators discovered that McKhoni had a history of hands-on sexual abuse of at least five minors. The investigation was led by the FBI Akron Resident Agency. Assistant United States Attorney Jennifer J. King led the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. title: Illegal possession of a firearm and machinegun leads to federal prison for two defendants in separate cases
body: Press Release Illegal possession of a firearm and machinegun leads to federal prison for two defendants in separate cases Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Georgia SAVANNAH, Georgia: Two defendants were sentenced in district court for charges including possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and possession of a machinegun. The sentences were imposed by U.S. District Court Chief Judge R. Stan Baker and announced by Margaret E. “Meg” Heap, U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Georgia. Orlando Marcus Williams , a/k/a “Orlando Green,” 35, of Savannah, was sentenced to 79 months in prison followed by three years of supervised release after pleading guilty to Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon. According to court documents and testimony, in October 2025, Williams was found sleeping in front of a hotel on West Fairmont Ave. and in possession of a firearm, a Glock, Model 17, 9 mm pistol. Savannah Police Department officers contacted the defendant who provided two different names, and SPD officers confirmed the defendant’s prior criminal history and that he was a convicted felon. Antonio Juan Milian , a/k/a “Junior,” 35, of Hinesville, was sentenced to 58 months in prison followed by three years of supervised release after pleading guilty to Possession of a Machinegun. According to court documents and testimony, in June 2023, a coordinated investigation carried out by U.S. Army Criminal Investigations Division (CID), Liberty County Sheriff’s Office (LCSO) Narcotics Unit, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) developed intelligence that Milian was selling firearms and narcotics in Liberty County. During an undercover operation in July 2023, Milian sold a machinegun conversion device (MCD) to an undercover LCSO deputy. A MCD allows a firearm to fire multiple rounds with one pull of the trigger, converting a semi-automatic firearm into a fully automatic machinegun. There is no parole in the federal system. Under federal law, it is prohibited for previously convicted felons to possess firearms or ammunition. “These sentences highlight the power of seamless law enforcement collaboration in targeting illegal gun possession,” said U.S. Attorney Heap. “Thanks to the proactive investigations by our local and federal law enforcement partners, these two dangerous individuals are now off the streets and facing significant time in federal prison. This office remains committed to holding gun offenders accountable and keeping our neighborhoods safe.” These cases were investigated by the U.S. Army CID, the ATF, Liberty County Sheriff’s Office, and the Savannah Police Department. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. These cases were prosecuted for the United States by Southern District of Georgia Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jennifer J. Kirkland, Bradley R. Thompson, and Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Karl I. Knoche. Contact For any questions, please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Office at (912) 652-4422. title: Justice Department Awards St. Louis more than $68M to Combat Violent Crime and Restore Law and Order Through Model Cities Initiative
body: Press Release Justice Department Awards St. Louis more than $68M to Combat Violent Crime and Restore Law and Order Through Model Cities Initiative Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs St. Louis Was Selected Out of Nearly 50 American Cities to Receive Federal Funding to Strengthen Law Enforcement and Enhance Public Safety. Today, the Justice Department awarded St. Louis, Missouri, more than $68 million through its Model Cities Initiative (MCI), a flagship effort to reduce violent crime, restore law and order, and strengthen public safety in communities across the country. “The Model Cities Initiative reflects the Trump Administration’s commitment to reducing crime across the country and ensuring the safety of every American,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “These cities are setting an example of proactive law enforcement that will strengthen the rule of law and improve public safety in their jurisdictions. As violent crime rates continue to fall to historic lows, the Department of Justice is redoubling our efforts to invest in local communities and keep American families safe.” St. Louis was selected, in large part, because of the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department's (SLMPD) significant progress in reducing violent crime through data-driven policing, innovative technology, and strong partnerships with federal law enforcement agencies. The department has reported year-to-date reductions of 21% in homicides, 25% in robberies, 14% in auto thefts, and 22% in juvenile shootings. Under the leadership of Police Commissioner Robert Tracy, SLMPD has expanded its use of advanced technologies, including gunshot detection systems and drones, to strengthen investigative capabilities, improve situational awareness, and enhance emergency response times. “All Missouri families deserve to feel safe in their communities, and strengthening public safety in St. Louis is critical to the success and prosperity of our entire state,” said Governor Mike Kehoe of Missouri. “We were proud to partner with the Trump Administration in securing this game-changing investment that will strengthen efforts to crack down on violent crime and support the brave men and women in law enforcement.” “I’m a proud St. Louisan, but for too long violent crime has tormented our communities and left families feeling unsafe,” said Senator Eric Schmitt of Missouri. “As Missouri’s Attorney General and now as a U.S. Senator, I have spent my career fighting for a safer Missouri, and I am so proud that St. Louis was one of the four cities chosen as part of the Model Cities Initiative to support our law enforcement officers and serve as an example for the rest of the nation. We’ve gotten far too used to seeing violence in our city’s headlines, but that doesn’t have to be our reality. I am grateful that President Trump, Attorney General Blanche, and the entire Trump Administration are focused on fighting crime, and I look forward to our continued efforts to make life better — and safer — in the Show-Me State.” “This federal investment in public safety strengthens our hand in the fight against violent crime in St. Louis, and it supports the work of those who do that job every day,” said Missouri Attorney General Hanaway. “We stand shoulder-to-shoulder with the men and women of the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, who carry the responsibility of placing themselves between our communities and harm with courage and resolve. “This public safety effort represents our unified commitment to hold violent offenders accountable, strengthen public confidence, and build a safer St. Louis for every family.” “The progress we’ve made in reducing violent crime belongs to our officers, our law enforcement partners and the St. Louis residents who work alongside us,” said St. Louis Metropolitan Police Chief Robert J. Tracy. “I’m grateful to Attorney General Todd Blanche and the Department of Justice for investing in that work. This funding will help us recruit and retain officers, give them better information when they respond to emergencies and equip detectives to solve more violent crimes. Our goal is to improve quality of life in every neighborhood and make St. Louis a safer city for all.” Image of Check Awarded to St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department Image of Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward, Jr. Image of $68 Million Check Awarded to Image of Check Awarded to St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department Through the Model Cities Initiative, St. Louis aims to build on this momentum by further expanding its use of cutting-edge public safety technologies, strengthening officer recruitment and retention efforts, and enhancing coordination among federal, state, and local law enforcement partners. Proposed investments include doubling the department's drone fleet, expanding gunshot detection coverage, modernizing its Real-Time Crime Center, and providing additional equipment and resources to frontline officers. Collectively, these efforts are intended to create a sustainable and replicable model for reducing violent crime, enhancing public safety, and improving the quality of life for St. Louis residents. The MCI takes a whole-of-city approach to public safety, bringing together law enforcement agencies, local government officials, and community partners to develop comprehensive strategies that address the unique public safety challenges facing their communities. The applications submitted by the four selected jurisdictions exemplified the innovative, forward-thinking approaches the Department sought through the initiative. While each jurisdiction faces unique public safety challenges and brings different priorities, resources, and starting points to the initiative, the Department is confident in the strength of their proposals and their commitment to achieving meaningful results. Despite differing approaches, all four jurisdictions demonstrated a shared determination to reduce violent crime and make their communities safer. Through the initiative, the Justice Department will work with each jurisdiction to finalize and implement its public safety plan. Funding will support a range of priorities, including hiring sworn and non-sworn law enforcement officers and other personnel to support enforcement, prosecution, and related public safety activities; adopting new and improved technology; purchasing or leasing equipment; enhancing forensic capabilities and capacity; and providing services to address mental health and substance use issues and reduce recidivism. The Justice Department announced the Model Cities Initiative in June 2026 to build on early successes in jurisdictions such as Memphis, Tennessee, and Washington, D.C., in reducing violence, crime, and disorder. The initiative directs nearly $300 million in federal resources toward comprehensive public safety strategies that strengthen law enforcement, improve coordination among public safety partners, and address the factors contributing to crime and recidivism. Through these investments, the Justice Department will work alongside local partners to implement sustainable public safety solutions and deliver measurable results. The four Model Cities will help advance the Administration’s efforts to reject the status quo of allowing crime and disorder to go unchecked and restore law, order, and safety to communities across the nation. Jacksonville, Florida; Jackson, Mississippi; and Baton Rouge, Louisiana, have additionally been selected to receive federal investments supporting innovative, comprehensive, locally driven strategies to combat crime and enhance coordination among federal, state, and local law enforcement partners. The specific departments funded are: Baton Rouge - East Baton Rouge Parish, Louisiana; Jackson - City of Jackson, Mississippi; Jacksonville - City of Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office; and St. Louis - St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department. Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component Office of the Attorney General Press Release Number: 26-1335

title: Springfield, Massachusetts Man Sentenced to 60 Months for Drug Trafficking and Maintaining a Drug Stash House
body: Press Release Springfield, Massachusetts Man Sentenced to 60 Months for Drug Trafficking and Maintaining a Drug Stash House Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Vermont USAVT.Press@usdoj.gov BURLINGTON – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Vermont stated that on October 29, 2026, Armando Robles, 33, of Springfield, Massachusetts, was sentenced by Chief United States District Judge Christina Reiss to a term of 60 months’ imprisonment to be followed by a 4-year term of supervised release. Robles previously pleaded guilty to possessing with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of cocaine and maintaining a drug-involved premises. According to court records, in the Spring of 2025, law enforcement conducted four controlled purchases of suspected narcotics from Robles at locations in and around Burlington, Vermont. Following the controlled purchases, on June 13, 2025, law enforcement executed a search at a residence in South Burlington, Vermont, which had been rented by Robles to facilitate his drug trafficking activity. Inside the residence, officers found nearly 600 grams of cocaine, more than 100 grams of cocaine base, approximately $1,400 in United States currency (including money from the most recent controlled purchase), and multiple cellular phones, including the one which had been used to arrange the controlled purchases. First Assistant United States Attorney Jonathan A. Ophardt commended the collaborative investigatory efforts of the Drug Enforcement Administration and Burlington Police Department. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Katherine Flynn. Robles was represented by Federal Public Defender Alejandro Fernandez. Contact Media Inquiries/Public Affairs Officer: (802) 651-8250 Updated November 9, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Vermont

title: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum
body: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum November 9, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT -NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX. Ryu Je-myung, vice minister of science and ICT , joined NVIDIA leaders to meet with over 20 Korean startups across foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and AI semiconductors. NVIDIA also announced an investment in Korean startup Point2 , with additional investments planned in Motif Technologies , RLWRLD and Upstage. Point2 Technology, an AI interconnect company, builds scalable, radio frequency-based interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offering an innovative alternative to conventional copper and optical interconnect solutions for AI cluster scale-up, delivering the reach, performance and efficiency needed for next-generation AI infrastructure. Motif Technologies , a Seoul-based AI lab, develops foundation models for building AI agents that carry out complex tasks, including Motif-3, a large language model released with open weights. RLWRLD, a physical AI startup based in San Francisco, Seoul and Tokyo, develops robotics foundation models that enable humanoid and industrial robots to perform complex real-world tasks that require five-finger dexterity, such as precisely inserting components, threading nuts onto bolts and kitting parts from moving conveyors. Upstage , a Korean enterprise AI company, develops Solar language models and document AI tools that help businesses extract information from complex documents, streamline workflows and build AI applications for everyday operations. The companies represent work across the full AI stack , from infrastructure to models to robotics applications. The planned investments build on NVIDIA’s work with Korea’s startup and venture community, including more than 1,000 Korea-based members of NVIDIA Inception , a program that helps startups grow with access to preferred pricing, technical expertise and opportunities for investor introductions. title: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA
body: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA November 8, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Tapping into the country’s strengths in manufacturing and engineering, NVIDIA is helping advance Korea’s physical AI ecosystem. The country’s industry leaders are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to everything from semiconductor manufacturing to robotics and autonomous vehicles. These efforts are helping bring physical AI from development into real-world production. Samsung Advances Semiconductor Engineering With Accelerated Computing and AI Physics Samsung Electronics is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to advance semiconductor innovation through accelerated computing and AI physics. The work spans materials research, process development and device engineering. In technology computer-aided design, Samsung is working with NVIDIA cuISS and NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate computations involving sparse linear systems. The collaboration also extends to GPU acceleration for process and optical simulations. In materials research, Samsung’s sMOL platform has run selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end with NVIDIA cuEST . Samsung is also exploring NVIDIA cuEquivariance to speed up tensor operations used in training and inference for atomistic AI models. Samsung is developing chip-scale thermal and mechanical analysis workflows with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo . In one AI homogenization case, combining AI-predicted effective material properties, coarser grids and GPU acceleration resulted in a roughly 1,600x speedup. Simulation time fell from about 18 hours for a fine-grid solve on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds for a GPU-accelerated coarse-grid solve. Looking ahead, NVIDIA Agent Toolkit could connect these simulation tools and AI models, helping future engineering agents run analyses and compare design options. Kakao Mobility Collaborates With NVIDIA to Advance Autonomous Driving Development Kakao Mobility plans to build on NVIDIA’s autonomous vehicle computing and safety technologies to advance development of a level 4 autonomous driving system. The work combines Kakao Mobility’s proprietary driving software and experience operating in Seoul’s Gangnam district with NVIDIA’s vehicle computing platform. Kakao Mobility plans to use NVIDIA Hyperion , a reference platform for vehicle sensors and compute, powered by NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor. It also plans to use NVIDIA Halos to support safety across the development and validation of its autonomous driving technology. Initial development is planned around Kia purpose-built vehicles, integrating Kakao Mobility’s autonomous driving software with NVIDIA technologies. The effort aims to support future level 4 mobility services in Korea. LG Electronics Advances Robot Learning and Factory Simulation NVIDIA and LG Electronics successfully demonstrated NVIDIA Isaac GR00T-powered robotic manipulation and manufacturing tasks using LG’s CLOiD robot in an actual manufacturing environment. The collaboration implemented a physical AI data flywheel connecting real-world data collection, NVIDIA Cosmos-based data augmentation, GR00T model training, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor onboard computing and simulation-based evaluation, establishing reusable workflows for continued development and validation of CLOiD’s robotic capabilities. The teams are using this work to refine a repeatable process for training, evaluating and improving robots for manufacturing. title: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA
body: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA Hyundai Motor Group and AIM Intelligence explore NVIDIA NemoClaw and OpenShell for secure enterprise agents, and LG AI Research opens API for ‘K-EXAONE-2.5’ trained on Nemotron datasets. November 8, 2026 by Nicola Sessions 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! As AI agents take on more work, they need capable open models and security that advances alongside them. Hyundai Motor Group is exploring NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and the NVIDIA OpenShell runtime, while AIM Intelligence is integrating its Starfort platform with NVIDIA OpenShell to support secure AI agents for employee productivity and enterprise workflows . A key component of the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform, OpenShell provides a secure runtime with sandboxed execution and policy-based controls to safeguard sensitive data, manage access to enterprise tools and govern autonomous agent actions. AIM Intelligence , a Korean AI security company, is integrating its Starfort agent control platform with NVIDIA OpenShell. The goal is to combine OpenShell’s runtime access controls with Starfort’s detection of malicious instructions and data leakage. The company is also considering a preliminary proof of concept for the public energy sector, with potential applications across enterprise, industrial and robotics environments. On the model side, LG AI Research is opening application programming interface access for K-EXAONE-2.5, developed using NVIDIA Nemotron datasets, including Nemotron-Personas-Korea . Nemotron-Personas-Korea is an open dataset of 7 million fully synthetic Korean personas, grounded in official Korean statistics, that model builders use to ground training data and evaluation in Korean contexts. NVIDIA Nemotron is a family of open models, datasets and techniques that help developers build specialized, efficient AI agents. Learn more about NVIDIA Nemotron open models and get started building secure agents with NVIDIA OpenShell . title: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration
body: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration November 8, 2026 by Jesse Clayton 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security. The collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, and includes NVIDIA training and certification programs, hackathons and technical seminars to strengthen GPU utilization. Through Korea’s AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will collaborate with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders, using NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize and scale AI inference. In addition, NVIDIA today announced a collaboration with SK Telecom and Rebellions, supported by MSIT, to advance sovereign AI infrastructure for Korean models and workloads with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion. Read more in the press release . title: November 9, 2026 - FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk For Immediate Release: November 09, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, the first factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor for use in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults following a recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (a stroke caused by a clot that did not originate in the heart) or a high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA), often called a “mini-stroke.” “Stroke is a leading cause of disability and death in the United States, and survivors are at risk of having another stroke,” said Hylton V. Joffe, M.D., MMSc, Director of the Office of Cardiology, Hematology, Endocrinology, and Nephrology in the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “Today’s approval represents a meaningful advance for patients and health care providers seeking a new option for secondary stroke prevention.” The effectiveness of Sunharbo was demonstrated in the OCEANIC-STROKE study , a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study that enrolled 12,327 adults. Participants had a recent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale ≤15) or high-risk TIA and were randomly assigned to Sunharbo or placebo within 72 hours of symptom onset. Both groups also received antiplatelet therapy. Sunharbo 50 mg once daily significantly reduced the risk of ischemic stroke by 26% compared to placebo over a median treatment of 14.2 months. The overall rate of major bleeding was similar between the Sunharbo and placebo groups but was increased with Sunharbo in patients older than 75 years and during the first 90 days of treatment. Gastrointestinal bleeding occurred more commonly with Sunharbo compared to placebo. The most frequently reported adverse reaction (occurring in 3% or greater of Sunharbo-treated patients) was diarrhea. Concomitant use with medicines that are combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers (such as carbamazepine) is not recommended because these medicines may decrease Sunharbo’s effectiveness. Sunharbo is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Sunharbo should be withheld at least 24 hours before elective surgery or invasive procedures and for at least 24 hours after thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke. Sunharbo is not approved for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation. The FDA granted Sunharbo Fast Track and Priority Review designations. The approval was granted to Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc., Whippany, N.J. Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

title: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production
body: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production November 8, 2026 by Amr Elmeleegy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom , K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research , Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies . As models grow beyond the capacity of a single GPU, they must be split across multiple GPUs, requiring careful coordination of request routing and communication to maintain performance. NVIDIA Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework built to deploy models in multi-node environments at data center scale. It handles this routing and communication to maximize inference performance. Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box. They help developers bring Korea’s open models into production faster and turn them into broadly accessible AI for All services. Learn more about NVIDIA Dynamo . body: November 6, 2026 PARIS —Last week, senior Treasury officials led a U.S. government delegation to the Financial Action Task Force’s(FATF) plenary meetings.  The FATF, the global standard-setting body for countering money laundering, terror financing, and proliferation financing, concluded its first Plenary under the United Kingdom presidency.  The FATF adopted the Mutual Evaluation Reports of the United States and Mexico, reiterated the call to impose countermeasures on Iran, agreed to publish a new report on scam centers, and agreed to accelerate global implementation of digital asset-related standards. STOPPING IRANIAN ILLICIT FINANCE Iran remains on the FATF’s blacklist, and the FATF called upon all nations to implement reimposed United Nations Security Council Resolutions related to Iran’s ongoing lack of compliance with its nuclear agreements. The FATF also reminded all jurisdictions to impose countermeasures on Iran to restrict correspondent banking, digital asset transactions, and business relationships with Iran. DISMANTLING SOUTHEAST ASIAN SCAM COMPOUNDS The FATF also adopted a landmark report examining the financial flows fueling scam compounds, laying the groundwork for a stronger, more coordinated global response to fraud.  Building on these findings, the FATF will advance concrete measures to use its full range of tools to drive more decisive action to disrupt these criminal networks, hold jurisdictions accountable for failing to address these risks, and protect victims and the global financial system.  Scams orchestrated at these compounds often target older and vulnerable Americans, and the Trump Administration has taken numerous sanctions actions to stop the fraud. ADVANCING THE DIGITAL ASSETS SECTOR The FATF also agreed to launch a targeted review of certain jurisdictions with longstanding deficiencies related to the virtual assets sector that heighten illicit finance risks.  This review will outline decision points for the next FATF plenary on what the FATF can do to ensure accountability for jurisdictions with systemic weaknesses that enable fraudsters, drug traffickers, and proliferators to launder funds through exchanges. Click here to read the Outcomes of the FATF Plenary, 6 November 2026. ###

title: Operation Economic Outcast Sanctions Eight Canadian Money Services Businesses Enabling Iranian Regime
body: November 6, 2026 Several of the Targets Also Worked with Narcotrafficker and Former Olympic Snowboarder Ryan Wedding WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated eight money services businesses based in Canada that enable the Iranian regime, sanctioned entities associated with the regime, and other illicit actors that move assets into and out of Iran.  These companies facilitate the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets to enable international transactions involving Iran.  Many of these businesses have facilitated transactions with sanctioned Iranian digital asset exchanges, as well as with digital asset addresses associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). “Canada cannot be a safe haven for illicit financial facilitators that provide sanctions evasion services to the Iranian regime and its proxies,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “Treasury will pursue and disrupt the Iranian regime’s financial channels anywhere in the world.” In August, Treasury launched Operation Economic Outcast to sever the economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime and its IRGC, including Tehran’s exploitation of cryptocurrency as a tool of choice for sanctions evasion.  Today’s designations are a continuation of Treasury’s comprehensive campaign to disrupt the regime’s exploitation of digital assets to fund terrorism, human rights abuses, and attacks on U.S. personnel and allies.  These designations also follow previous OFAC sanctions on digital asset exchanges that have moved digital assets abroad on behalf of the Iranian regime, including the June 2, 2026 designations of Iranian exchanges Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex , and the August 7, 2026 designations of Aban Tether Exchange and SHPS Shelbit (Shelbit), which operates the Shelbit Exchange that has moved millions of dollars on behalf of the IRGC. Today’s action was coordinated with the Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and FINTRAC, Canada’s financial intelligence unit.  This action is also taken in coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and reflects the Trump Administration’s whole-of-government effort to combat the illicit use of digital assets for drug trafficking.  Several of the entities designated in this action have also worked with the OFAC-sanctioned Canadian drug trafficker Ryan Wedding .  Wedding has used money exchange businesses in the Vancouver and Toronto areas to launder billions of dollars in drug proceeds.  He has used couriers to transport bulk cash to those firms, which convert the funds to digital assets to send abroad.  Wedding was apprehended in January 2026 , but he worked with several of the money services businesses designated today to transfer millions of dollars’ worth of digital assets prior to being taken into U.S. custody. Today’s designations are imposed pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian digital asset sector among other key sectors of the Iranian economy.  The Department of the Treasury will continue to target not only the Iranian digital asset ecosystem, but also international entities and actors that help facilitate it.  For more information on sanctions risk associated with Iranian digital asset exchanges, please see FAQ 1250 and FAQ 1257 . CANADIAN MONEY SERVICES BUSINESSES: AN IRANIAN SANCTIONS EVASION CHANNEL Canada is home to hundreds of money services businesses that enable the movement of funds into and out of Iran, both through cash-based value transfer systems and by converting cash into digital assets to send across borders.  The entities designated in this action allow sanctioned Iranian entities to use their services, thereby providing the Iranian regime with financial lifelines and the ability to continue to finance terrorism and proxy groups.  Many of these entities also receive and launder funds associated with other criminal activity.  Although Canadian and international media sources have highlighted the sanctions evasion and terrorist financing-related risks that certain of these money services businesses pose, the entities designated today remain operational.  Several of these entities have changed their business names and addresses in an attempt to evade detection and enforcement actions. Diverse Trade Inc, doing business as Million Exchange , is an Ontario-based money services business that advertises the ability to exchange Iranian rials for other currencies, as well as the management of digital assets for customers.  Digital asset addresses associated with Million Exchange have sent the equivalent of hundreds of thousands of dollars to addresses associated with the IRGC or other terrorism-related addresses.  Million Exchange has also laundered drug proceeds by using cash generated from drug sales to purchase digital assets to send back to drug dealers.  Wedding has laundered drug proceeds through Million Exchange using this method, and has also directed sending certain digital assets abroad that Million Exchange purchased with drug-related cash. 1380079 BC Limited is a British Columbia-based money services business that does business as Amin Exchange and that facilitates currency transfers between Iran and Canada, as well as the purchase and sale of digital assets. Top PC Technician Inc , which is a closely associated affiliate of 1380079 BC Limited, operates in Ontario as a money services business and also does business as the same Amin Exchange.  Digital asset addresses associated with Amin Exchange have received hundreds of thousands of dollars from Shelbit.  Amin Exchange has laundered millions of dollars in drug proceeds in Canada at locations in Toronto, Vancouver, and Montreal.  Amin Exchange in Vancouver has laundered drug proceeds for Wedding.  The company has received the proceeds in cash and transferred them into digital assets, which Wedding has directed to be sent abroad. NIA Nations Currency Ltd ( NIA Nations ) is a British Columbia-based money services business that advertises digital asset exchange services and the ability to transfer money from Iran to Canada.  Digital asset addresses associated with NIA Nations have transacted with addresses associated with the IRGC and sanctioned Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges, including Nobitex, Wallex, Ramzinex, and Bitpin. 2397639 Ontario Ltd, doing business as Farah Exchange , advertises itself as an Iranian exchange operating in Canada, offering foreign exchange and digital assets.  A digital asset address associated with Farah Exchange has conducted hundreds of thousands of dollars’ worth of transactions with sanctioned Iran-related exchanges Shelbit and Wallex.  Farah Exchange has also sent thousands of dollars in digital assets to addresses associated with terrorism and millions of dollars in digital assets to addresses associated with Wedding. CCC Inc and B Galaxy Inc are two Ontario companies that operate in the same location and provide currency exchange and digital asset exchange services.  A CCC Inc website offers the buying and selling of digital currencies, and indicates it is licensed in Iran and Canada.  A digital asset address associated with CCC Inc has received hundreds of thousands of dollars in digital assets from addresses associated with terrorism.  B Galaxy Inc, doing business as Cryptoyal, advertises unlimited amounts of digital assets in exchange for Iranian currencies. Darvish Exchange is an Ontario-based money services business that advertises the ability to exchange Bitcoin for Iranian rials.  A digital asset address associated with Darvish Exchange has transacted with sanctioned Iranian exchanges Nobitex, Wallex, Aban Tether Exchange, and Shelbit. OFAC is designating Million Exchange, 1380079 BC Limited, Top PC Technician Inc, NIA Nations, Farah Exchange, CCC Inc, B Galaxy Inc, and Darvish Exchange pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the digital asset sector of the Iranian economy. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency.  In the case of sanctions related to Iran, OFAC is employing all available statutory, regulatory, and policy tools to resolve the persistent national emergencies posed by Iran, which has not changed its behavior to align with U.S. national security and foreign policy objectives.  OFAC sanctions determinations, including removal determinations, are made consistent with Administration foreign policy and national security policies and priorities.  For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List . Click here for more information on the persons designated and any property identified as blocked property today.

title: Operation Economic Outcast Severs MEXC Global’s Access to the U.S. Financial System
body: November 6, 2026 CVC Exchanger Facilitated at Least $16 Billion in Illicit Finance, Including for IRGC-Qods Force WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued an order effectively cutting off MEXC Global’s access to the U.S. financial system. MEXC Global is a convertible virtual currency (CVC) exchanger that has facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit transactions connected to Iranian, North Korean, and Russian sanctions evasion, as well as cybercrime, including by transacting directly with sanctioned actors. “Financial institutions cannot have it both ways: Either you support the Iranian regime, or you have access to the U.S. financial system,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “Treasury will continue to sever the Iranian regime’s economic lifelines and thwart its desperate attempts to circumvent U.S. sanctions using digital assets.” FinCEN’s order prevents U.S. financial institutions from processing funds transfers involving MEXC Global. MEXC Global: A Hub for Sanctioned Actors MEXC Global was founded in 2018, and as of September 2026, processed more than $1 billion in daily transactions and maintained approximately $5 billion in reserves.  It is one of the top 20 largest CVC exchangers in the world.  The platform offers trading in more than 50 currencies and access to more than 3,000 different cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets. Although the platform claims to maintain anti-money laundering (AML) and customer identification and verification policies—and explicitly prohibits use by or on behalf of individuals in certain jurisdictions, including Iran and North Korea—severe deficiencies in its AML controls have allowed it to facilitate transactions for individuals or entities in those prohibited jurisdictions, making it a significant conduit for illicit finance. Between May 2021 and May 2026, MEXC Global facilitated the movement of at least $16 billion in funds connected to sanctions evasion, cybercrime, and other illicit activity.  This includes nearly $1.5 billion in transactions linked to Russian sanctions evasion, including $232 million in direct transactions with U.S.-, EU-, and UK-sanctioned entities, making MEXC Global of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance.  In fact, MEXC Global was still processing transactions with sanctioned Russian entity Garantex, and its successor Grinex, as recently as June 2026—more than four years after Garantex’s April 2022 designation by Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).  MEXC Global also facilitated at least $26 million in transactions benefitting the Russia-based, OFAC-sanctioned A7 sanctions evasion network and processed almost $200 million in transactions connected to the A7A5 stablecoin, a store of value used by the A7 Network to help clients evade sanctions. MEXC Global has not only facilitated Russian illicit finance but has also served as a hub for other types of illicit financial activity, including Iranian and DPRK sanctions evasion, ransomware and scam payments, and Russian and other darknet market activity.  Between May 2021 and May 2026, MEXC Global had sent or received approximately $1 billion in direct transactions with more than 40 identified Iranian CVC exchangers, some of which are subject to U.S. and international sanctions.  In the same period, MEXC Global facilitated approximately $22 million in transactions for the OFAC- and EU-sanctioned Central Bank of Iran and the OFAC-, UK-, and EU-sanctioned Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and its Qods Force. IMPLICATIONS OF TODAY’S ACTION Today’s action will protect the U.S. financial system from the significant illicit finance threats posed by MEXC Global.  The order, issued pursuant to section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act, prohibits U.S. financial institutions from engaging in any transmittal of funds from or to MEXC Global.  Violations of this order may result in civil or criminal penalties.  The order does not modify existing obligations under the Bank Secrecy Act (including Suspicious Activity Report filing requirements) or sanctions administered by OFAC.  The order is effective 30 days after publication in the Federal Register . Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.  As highlighted in FinCEN’s recent Bulletin , this includes information about violations of the Bank Secrecy Act or OFAC-administered sanctions programs that may involve the use of Iranian proxies and facilitators operating outside of Iran. FinCEN’s order can be found here . For questions about FinCEN’s order, please contact FinCEN at http://www.fincen.gov/contact . ###

title: READOUT: Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent’s Call with China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng
body: November 6, 2026 WASHINGTON — Today, Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent and United States Trade Representative Jameison Greer spoke with Vice Premier He Lifeng of the People’s Republic of China to discuss the bilateral economic relationship and implementation of the Busan arrangement. The two officials reaffirmed the value of maintaining direct and candid communication. Secretary Bessent emphasized the importance of China fully and immediately implementing its commitments made in Busan and raised concerns about recent Chinese actions. He underscored that continued progress depends on concrete results and that the United States will closely assess China’s implementation of the arrangement. Secretary Bessent reiterated the Trump Administration’s commitment to pursuing trade and economic policies that benefit American workers, farmers, and businesses and strengthen U.S. economic and national security. ###

title: National Republican Congressional Committee v. Brown
Treasury Targets Global Scam Networks and the Corporate Infrastructure That Enables Them
body: November 5, 2026 WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned four individuals and 41 entities that support the business network of Prince Group Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO) previously sanctioned by the United States for its role in cyber-enabled fraud, money laundering, and human trafficking.  Additionally, OFAC designated a Malaysian individual who defrauded U.S. victims by managing a network of Africa-based scammers. “Cyber scam syndicates continue to steal billions of dollars from American victims while relying on sophisticated international business networks to launder their illicit proceeds,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “Treasury remains committed to dismantling every layer of these organizations—from their leadership to the corporate structures and financial facilitators that enable them to operate with impunity.” Today’s action builds on OFAC’s October 14, 2025 and June 23, 2026 designations targeting Prince Group leadership, affiliated companies, and financial facilitators. Prince Group TCO-affiliated actors have generated billions of dollars in illicit proceeds through sophisticated cyber-enabled fraud schemes, including digital asset investment scams, romance scams, and other online fraud that have victimized Americans and individuals around the world.  Many of these operations have been linked to scam compounds in Southeast Asia that rely on trafficked and coerced workers, while criminal proceeds are laundered through complex networks of offshore companies and financial facilitators.  The newly designated individuals and entities have helped sustain Prince Group TCO’s illicit global operations after the October 2025 and June 2026 designations by managing offshore corporate structures, concealing beneficial ownership, facilitating commercial activities, and providing administrative and financial services to senior Prince Group TCO executives.  Individuals targeted today have participated in activities to evade previous sanctions targeting the Prince Group TCO, including the transfer of property and owning of companies with or on behalf of previously designated Prince Group TCO leaders.  Today’s action further targets the corporate and financial infrastructure that has enabled Prince Group TCO leaders to conceal assets, evade prior sanctions, and maintain access to the international financial system. These actions are in furtherance of President Trump’s Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 of March 6, 2026, “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” which orders the U.S. government to unleash every available tool to stop foreign-backed criminal networks that exploit vulnerable Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled fraud, and extortion.  OFAC is designating 45 targets pursuant to E.O. 13581 (“Blocking Property of Transnational Criminal Organizations”), as amended by E.O. 13863 (“E.O. 13581, as amended”), and one target pursuant to E.O. 13694 (“Blocking the Property of Certain Persons Engaging in Significant Malicious Cyber-Enabled Activities”), as further amended by E.O. 13757, E.O. 14144, and E.O. 14306 (“E.O. 13694, as further amended”). These actions are in coordination with the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s New York and Honolulu Field Offices, Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, and the U.S. Attorney’s office for the District of Alaska.  OFAC also appreciates the cooperation of the British Virgin Islands Financial Investigation Agency (BVI FIA) and the United Kingdom’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), whose timely assistance and information sharing were instrumental in supporting this sanctions action. TARGETING THOSE WHO EXPLOIT AMERICANS THROUGH FRAUD Prince Group TCO-affiliated actors have targeted victims in the United States and around the world through sophisticated cyber-enabled fraud schemes, including digital asset investment scams, romance scams, and other online financial fraud.  These schemes rely on deception and social engineering to persuade victims to transfer funds or digital assets to criminally controlled accounts, generating billions of dollars in illicit proceeds. Many of these operations are carried out from large-scale scam compounds in Southeast Asia, where trafficked and coerced workers are forced to perpetrate online fraud against victims across the globe.  Criminal proceeds are subsequently laundered through an international network of shell companies, offshore holding companies, financial facilitators, and digital asset transactions, allowing transnational criminal organizations to conceal the origin of illicit funds and integrate them into the legitimate financial system. Today’s action builds on Treasury’s ongoing efforts to dismantle not only the leadership of these criminal enterprises, but also the overseas corporate infrastructure and professional facilitators that enable them to target American victims, move illicit proceeds across jurisdictions, and evade law enforcement.  The Prince Group TCO has developed an extensive network of companies spanning multiple jurisdictions to support its commercial interests and conceal assets connected to its criminal enterprise.  Rather than operating through a single corporate structure, senior Prince Group TCO executives have relied on layers of offshore holding companies, foreign entities, nominee directors, and corporate service providers to maintain control over assets while obscuring beneficial ownership.  Today’s designations target key components of that network, including companies and individuals that have facilitated corporate administration, managed offshore entities, and provided business services to senior Prince Group TCO officials.  These facilitators have played an important role in enabling the Prince Group TCO to access the international financial system and preserve the appearance of legitimate commercial activity. DISMANTLING THE PRINCE GROUP’S CORPORATE INFRASTRUCTURE Qiu Yong is a key Prince Group TCO member who controls multiple BVI and Hong Kong companies on behalf of Prince Group TCO, and who has served as an employee of a company controlled by Prince Group TCO’s leader, Chen Zhi.  Chen Zhi was designated on October 14, 2025. Qiu Yong holds passports from multiple jurisdictions, including Cambodia, St. Lucia, and Türkiye, and is the beneficial owner of multiple BVI-based companies that control a network of Hong Kong companies involved in money lending and other business ventures. Hong Kong-based companies Premium Financial Limited (Premium Financial) and Solar Scape Financial Limited (Solar Scape Financial) are money lending companies ultimately owned by Qiu Yong through BVI-registered Sun Speed Holdings Limited (Sun Speed Holdings) and Solar Scape Limited (Solar Scape), respectively.  Hong Kong-based Direct Astute HK Limited (Direct Astute HK) is ultimately owned by Qiu Yong via BVI-registered Direct Astute Limited (Direct Astute).  Hong Kong-based Glad Vast Limited (Glad Vast), Glad Sparkle Limited (Glad Sparkle), and Glad Harvest Limited (Glad Harvest) are linked to the wine industry and are ultimately owned by Qiu Yong through BVI-registered Glad Glory Limited (Glad Glory). Per Hong Kong media reporting, Qiu was involved in the distribution and sale of wine across Hong Kong and Macao, illustrating Prince Group TCO’s reach into ostensibly legitimate businesses.  Qiu is also the beneficial owner of BVI-registered shelf companies Victory Flora Limited (Victora Flora), Win Applause Limited (Win Applause), Celestial Drive Limited (Celestial Drive), and Sino Sagacious Limited (Sino Sagacious). Hong Kong-based Zhao Mengyao , a.k.a. Amy Zhao, is Qiu Yong’s personal assistant and serves as company secretary and co-director of multiple Hong Kong-based companies ultimately controlled by Qiu Yong.  Zhao Mengyao and Qiu Yong are both shareholders of Hong Kong-based Mighty Divine Trust Hong Kong Limited (Mighty Divine Trust), a company directed by Zhou Yun, an individual previously identified by OFAC as a financial assistant and wealth manager for Prince Group TCO leader Chen Zhi.  Mighty Divine Trust and Zhou Yun were both designated on October 14, 2025. Qiu Yong is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Prince Group TCO.  Premium Financial, Solar Scape Financial, Sun Speed Holdings, Solar Scape, Direct Astute HK, Direct Astute, Glad Vast, Glad Sparkle, Glad Harvest, Glad Glory, Victora Flora, Win Applause, Celestial Drive, and Sino Sagacious are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or to having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Qiu Yong.   Zhao Mengyao is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Qiu Yong. OFAC is also targeting two individuals who are holding property for, or co-directing companies with, Prince Group TCO executive Chen Bo, who was designated on June 23, 2026. This includes Chen Bo’s wife, Cambodian national He Yujing , and Cambodian Prince Group TCO associate Visal Pang . Since OFAC’s action in October 2025, Chen Bo has transferred ownership of his Tokyo mansion to He Yujing, who also owns the Cambodian company Super Light Speed Kh Technology Co., Ltd .  Cambodia-based Visal Pang controls eleven Cambodian companies, several of which he co-directs with Chen Bo: Cambodia First Unite Construction Group (CFU Group) Co., Ltd., First Unite International Logistics Co., Ltd., First Unite Networks Entertainment Co., Ltd., First Unite Property Co., Ltd., First Unite Decoration (Cambodia) Co., Ltd., Cambodian First Unite Construction Machinery Co., Ltd., Linkedus Technology Co., Ltd., Cambo Duty Free Merchandise Co., Ltd., Marco Polo Hotel Co., Ltd., U-Life Go Now Co., Ltd. , and U-Life Kh Super App Co., Ltd. Visal Pang was also designated by the United Kingdom on March 26, 2026. Chen Bo remains in control of eleven Cambodian companies: Asian Welfare Lotteries Co., Ltd. , CB General Insurance PLC. , Cambodian Resource Energy Development Co., Ltd. , Cambodian Unite Wei Ye Investment Co. , DT Zhi Zao, Co., Ltd. , First Aquatic Industrial Co., Ltd. , Mo Net Beauty Co., Ltd. , Prince International Airlines Co., Ltd. , Richeng Property Developer Co., Ltd. , Tian Xu International Technology Plc. , and ZHX Printing Equipment Cambodia Co., Ltd . He Yujing is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of Prince Group TCO.  Super Light Speed Kh Technology Co., Ltd is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, He Yujing. Visal Pang is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of Prince Group TCO.  Cambodia First Unite Construction Group (CFU Group) Co., Ltd., First Unite International Logistics Co., Ltd., First Unite Networks Entertainment Co., Ltd., First Unite Property Co., Ltd., First Unite Decoration (Cambodia) Co., Ltd., Cambodian First Unite Construction Machinery Co., Ltd., Linkedus Technology Co., Ltd., Cambo Duty Free Merchandise Co., Ltd., Marco Polo Hotel Co., Ltd., U-Life Go Now Co., Ltd., and U-Life Kh Super App Co., Ltd. are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Visal Pang. Asian Welfare Lotteries Co., Ltd., CB General Insurance PLC., Cambodian Resource Energy Development Co., Ltd., Cambodian Unite Wei Ye Investment Co., DT Zhi Zao, Co., Ltd., First Aquatic Industrial Co., Ltd., Mo Net Beauty Co., Ltd., Prince International Airlines Co., Ltd., Richeng Property Developer Co., Ltd., Tian Xu International Technology Plc., and ZHX Printing Equipment Cambodia Co., Ltd. are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Chen Bo. On June 23, 2026, OFAC designated Prince Group TCO associate Dai An, a high-level leader in the Prince Group TCO.  Dai is the majority owner of Singapore-based Chen Hua Holdings Pte Ltd (Chen Hua Holdings) and serves as director for Mauritius-based Meritwise Group Public Ltd (Meritwise Group) and Malaysia-based Greenmeadows Properties Sdn Bhd (Greenmeadows). Chen Hua Holdings, Meritwise Group, and Greenmeadows are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or to have acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Dai An. Singapore-based Greenbay Multi Media Pte Ltd (Greenbay Multi Media) is 100 percent owned by OFAC-designated Prince Group TCO executive Thet Li.  Thet Li was designated by OFAC on October 14, 2025. Greenbay Multi Media is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13581, as amended, for being owned or controlled by, or to have acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Thet Li. SANCTIONS AGAINST FACILITATOR OF MADAGASCAR-BASED SCAM NETWORK Chui Kok Wa (Chui) led an extensive network of scammers located in Madagascar that targeted Americans with scams, including defrauding Americans of digital assets.  The scammers led by Chui exploited cyber-enabled technologies, including cryptocurrencies and digital systems and technologies, to defraud numerous Americans of over $400,000 equivalent, thereby materially contributing to the cybercrime and scam center threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economic health of the United States.  Chui’s network garnered sympathy from vulnerable victims in order to misappropriate their funds for the private financial gain of his network. OFAC is designating Chui Kok Wa pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being responsible for or complicit in, or having engaged in, directly or indirectly, cyber-enabled activities originating from, or directed by persons located, in whole or in substantial part, outside the United States that are reasonably likely to result in, or have materially contributed to, a threat to the national security, foreign policy, or economic health or financial stability of the United States, and that have the purpose of or involve causing a misappropriation of funds or economic resources, intellectual property, proprietary or business confidential information, personal identifiers, or financial information for commercial or competitive advantage or private financial gain. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S.  persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons. The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List .
